Homage to the Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Fully Awakened One

# Abhidhamma Piṭaka ^abhidhamma-0

## Book of Analysis ^2-0

### Analysis of the Aggregates ^2-1-0

#### Discourse Classification ^2-1-1-0

1. The five aggregates: the aggregate of material form, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations, the aggregate of consciousness. ^2-1

##### The Aggregate of Material Form ^2-1-1-1-0

2. Herein, what is the aggregate of material form? Whatever material form there is — past, future, or present; internal or external; coarse or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near — all of that, gathered and grouped together as one: this is called the aggregate of material form. ^2-2

3. Herein, what is past material form? Material form that has ceased, disappeared, changed, gone, completely vanished — having arisen and then passed away — belonging to the past, counted as belonging to the past, namely the four great elements and material form derived from the four great elements: this is called past material form.
Herein, what is future material form? Material form that is not born, has not come to be, has not been generated, has not been produced, has not been brought into being, has not appeared, has not arisen, has not co-arisen, has not come up, has not originated, belonging to the future, counted as belonging to the future, namely the four great elements and material form derived from the four great elements: this is called future material form.
Herein, what is present material form? Material form that is born, has come to be, has been generated, has been produced, has been brought into being, has appeared, has arisen, has co-arisen, has come up, has originated, belonging to the present, counted as belonging to the present, namely the four great elements and material form derived from the four great elements: this is called present material form. ^2-3

4. Herein, what is internal material form? Material form belonging internally, individually, exclusively, and personally, to this or that being, and clung to — namely the four great elements and material form derived from the four great elements: this is called internal material form.
Herein, what is external material form? Material form belonging internally, individually, exclusively, and personally, to this or that other being or other person, and clung to — namely the four great elements and material form derived from the four great elements: this is called external material form. ^2-4

5. Herein, what is coarse material form? The eye sense-field ... the tangible sense-field: this is called coarse material form.
Herein, what is subtle material form? The faculty of femininity ... solid food: this is called subtle material form. ^2-5

6. Herein, what is inferior material form? Material form that is looked down on, despised, scorned, treated with contempt, disregarded by this or that being — considered inferior, deemed inferior, regarded as inferior, unwished-for, unwanted, displeasing — namely sights, sounds, smells, tastes, and tangibles: this is called inferior material form.
Herein, what is superior material form? Material form that is not looked down on, not despised, not scorned, not treated with contempt, not disregarded, but is honored by this or that being — considered superior, deemed superior, regarded as superior, wished-for, wanted, pleasing — namely sights, sounds, smells, tastes, and tangibles: this is called superior material form. But material form should also be seen as inferior or superior only in comparison with this or that other material form. ^2-6

7. Herein, what is far material form? The faculty of femininity ... solid food, and whatever other material form there is that is not close by, not near at hand, far, not nearby: this is called far material form.
Herein, what is near material form? The eye sense-field ... the tangible sense-field, and whatever other material form there is that is close by, near at hand, not far, nearby: this is called near material form. But material form should also be seen as far or near only in comparison with this or that other material form. ^2-7

##### The Aggregate of Feeling ^2-1-1-2-0

8. Herein, what is the aggregate of feeling? Whatever feeling there is — past, future, or present; internal or external; coarse or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near — all of that, gathered and grouped together as one: this is called the aggregate of feeling. ^2-8

9. Herein, what is past feeling? Feeling that has ceased, disappeared, changed, gone, completely vanished — having arisen and then passed away — belonging to the past, counted as belonging to the past, namely pleasant feeling, painful feeling, and neutral feeling: this is called past feeling.
Herein, what is future feeling? Feeling that is not born, has not come to be, has not been generated, has not been produced, has not been brought into being, has not appeared, has not arisen, has not co-arisen, has not come up, has not originated, belonging to the future, counted as belonging to the future, namely pleasant feeling, painful feeling, and neutral feeling: this is called future feeling.
Herein, what is present feeling? Feeling that is born, has come to be, has been generated, has been produced, has been brought into being, has appeared, has arisen, has co-arisen, has come up, has originated, belonging to the present, counted as belonging to the present, namely pleasant feeling, painful feeling, and neutral feeling: this is called present feeling. ^2-9

10. Herein, what is internal feeling? Feeling belonging internally, individually, exclusively, and personally, to this or that being — namely pleasant feeling, painful feeling, and neutral feeling: this is called internal feeling.
Herein, what is external feeling? Feeling belonging internally, individually, exclusively, and personally, to this or that other being or other person — namely pleasant feeling, painful feeling, and neutral feeling: this is called external feeling. ^2-10

11. Herein, what is coarse feeling, what is subtle feeling? Unwholesome feeling is coarse, wholesome-and-neutral feeling is subtle. Wholesome-and-unwholesome feeling is coarse, neutral feeling is subtle. Painful feeling is coarse, pleasant and neutral feeling are subtle. Pleasant-and-painful feeling is coarse, neutral feeling is subtle. The feeling of one not in an attainment is coarse, the feeling of one in an attainment is subtle. Feeling with mental taints is coarse, feeling free of mental taints is subtle. But feeling should also be seen as coarse or subtle only in comparison with this or that other feeling. ^2-11

12. Herein, what is inferior feeling, what is superior feeling? Unwholesome feeling is inferior, wholesome-and-neutral feeling is superior. Wholesome-and-unwholesome feeling is inferior, neutral feeling is superior. Painful feeling is inferior, pleasant and neutral feeling are superior. Pleasant-and-painful feeling is inferior, neutral feeling is superior. The feeling of one not in an attainment is inferior, the feeling of one in an attainment is superior. Feeling with mental taints is inferior, feeling free of mental taints is superior. But feeling should also be seen as inferior or superior only in comparison with this or that other feeling. ^2-12

13. Herein, what is far feeling? Unwholesome feeling is far from wholesome-and-neutral feeling; wholesome-and-neutral feeling is far from unwholesome feeling; wholesome feeling is far from unwholesome-and-neutral feeling; unwholesome-and-neutral feeling is far from wholesome feeling; neutral feeling is far from wholesome-and-unwholesome feeling; wholesome-and-unwholesome feeling is far from neutral feeling. Painful feeling is far from pleasant and neutral feeling; pleasant and neutral feeling are far from painful feeling; pleasant feeling is far from painful and neutral feeling; painful and neutral feeling are far from pleasant feeling; neutral feeling is far from pleasant-and-painful feeling; pleasant-and-painful feeling is far from neutral feeling. The feeling of one not in an attainment is far from the feeling of one in an attainment; the feeling of one in an attainment is far from the feeling of one not in an attainment. Feeling with mental taints is far from feeling free of mental taints; feeling free of mental taints is far from feeling with mental taints: this is called far feeling.
Herein, what is near feeling? Unwholesome feeling is near unwholesome feeling; wholesome feeling is near wholesome feeling; neutral feeling is near neutral feeling. Painful feeling is near painful feeling; pleasant feeling is near pleasant feeling; neutral feeling is near neutral feeling. The feeling of one not in an attainment is near the feeling of one not in an attainment; the feeling of one in an attainment is near the feeling of one in an attainment. Feeling with mental taints is near feeling with mental taints; feeling free of mental taints is near feeling free of mental taints. This is called near feeling. But feeling should also be seen as far or near only in comparison with this or that other feeling. ^2-13

##### The Aggregate of Perception ^2-1-1-3-0

14. Herein, what is the aggregate of perception? Whatever perception there is — past, future, or present; internal or external; coarse or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near — all of that, gathered and grouped together as one: this is called the aggregate of perception. ^2-14

15. Herein, what is past perception? Perception that has ceased, disappeared, changed, gone, completely vanished — having arisen and then passed away — belonging to the past, counted as belonging to the past, namely perception born of eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact: this is called past perception.
Herein, what is future perception? Perception that is not born, has not come to be, has not been generated, has not been produced, has not been brought into being, has not appeared, has not arisen, has not co-arisen, has not come up, has not originated, belonging to the future, counted as belonging to the future, namely perception born of eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact: this is called future perception.
Herein, what is present perception? Perception that is born, has come to be, has been generated, has been produced, has been brought into being, has appeared, has arisen, has co-arisen, has come up, has originated, belonging to the present, counted as belonging to the present, namely perception born of eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact: this is called present perception. ^2-15

16. Herein, what is internal perception? Perception belonging internally, individually, exclusively, and personally, to this or that being — namely perception born of eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact: this is called internal perception.
Herein, what is external perception? Perception belonging internally, individually, exclusively, and personally, to this or that other being or other person — namely perception born of eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact: this is called external perception. ^2-16

17. Herein, what is coarse perception, what is subtle perception? Perception born of contact with resistance is coarse, perception born of contact with a mere designation is subtle. Unwholesome perception is coarse, wholesome-and-neutral perception is subtle. Wholesome-and-unwholesome perception is coarse, neutral perception is subtle. Perception joined with painful feeling is coarse, perception joined with pleasant and neutral feeling is subtle. Perception joined with pleasant-and-painful feeling is coarse, perception joined with neutral feeling is subtle. The perception of one not in an attainment is coarse, the perception of one in an attainment is subtle. Perception with mental taints is coarse, perception free of mental taints is subtle. But perception should also be seen as coarse or subtle only in comparison with this or that other perception. ^2-17

18. Herein, what is inferior perception, what is superior perception? Unwholesome perception is inferior, wholesome-and-neutral perception is superior. Wholesome-and-unwholesome perception is inferior, neutral perception is superior. Perception joined with painful feeling is inferior, perception joined with pleasant and neutral feeling is superior. Perception joined with pleasant-and-painful feeling is inferior, perception joined with neutral feeling is superior. The perception of one not in an attainment is inferior, the perception of one in an attainment is superior. Perception with mental taints is inferior, perception free of mental taints is superior. But perception should also be seen as inferior or superior only in comparison with this or that other perception. ^2-18

19. Herein, what is far perception? Unwholesome perception is far from wholesome-and-neutral perception; wholesome-and-neutral perception is far from unwholesome perception; wholesome perception is far from unwholesome-and-neutral perception; unwholesome-and-neutral perception is far from wholesome perception. Neutral perception is far from wholesome-and-unwholesome perception; wholesome-and-unwholesome perception is far from neutral perception. Perception joined with painful feeling is far from perception joined with pleasant and neutral feeling; perception joined with pleasant and neutral feeling is far from perception joined with painful feeling; perception joined with pleasant feeling is far from perception joined with painful and neutral feeling; perception joined with painful and neutral feeling is far from perception joined with pleasant feeling; perception joined with neutral feeling is far from perception joined with pleasant-and-painful feeling; perception joined with pleasant-and-painful feeling is far from perception joined with neutral feeling. The perception of one not in an attainment is far from the perception of one in an attainment; the perception of one in an attainment is far from the perception of one not in an attainment. Perception with mental taints is far from perception free of mental taints; perception free of mental taints is far from perception with mental taints: this is called far perception.
Herein, what is near perception? Unwholesome perception is near unwholesome perception; wholesome perception is near wholesome perception; neutral perception is near neutral perception. Perception joined with painful feeling is near perception joined with painful feeling; perception joined with pleasant feeling is near perception joined with pleasant feeling; perception joined with neutral feeling is near perception joined with neutral feeling. The perception of one not in an attainment is near the perception of one not in an attainment; the perception of one in an attainment is near the perception of one in an attainment. Perception with mental taints is near perception with mental taints; perception free of mental taints is near perception free of mental taints. This is called near perception. But perception should also be seen as far or near only in comparison with this or that other perception. ^2-19

##### The Aggregate of Formations ^2-1-1-4-0

20. Herein, what is the aggregate of formations? Whatever formations there are — past, future, or present; internal or external; coarse or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near — all of that, gathered and grouped together as one: this is called the aggregate of formations. ^2-20

21. Herein, what are past formations? Formations that have ceased, disappeared, changed, gone, completely vanished — having arisen and then passed away — belonging to the past, counted as belonging to the past, namely intention born of eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact: these are called past formations.
Herein, what are future formations? Formations that are not born, have not come to be, have not been generated, have not been produced, have not been brought into being, have not appeared, have not arisen, have not co-arisen, have not come up, have not originated, belonging to the future, counted as belonging to the future, namely intention born of eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact: these are called future formations.
Herein, what are present formations? Formations that are born, have come to be, have been generated, have been produced, have been brought into being, have appeared, have arisen, have co-arisen, have come up, have originated, belonging to the present, counted as belonging to the present, namely intention born of eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact: these are called present formations. ^2-21

22. Herein, what are internal formations? Formations belonging internally, individually, exclusively, and personally, to this or that being — namely intention born of eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact: these are called internal formations.
Herein, what are external formations? Formations belonging internally, individually, exclusively, and personally, to this or that other being or other person — namely intention born of eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact: these are called external formations. ^2-22

23. Herein, what are coarse formations, what are subtle formations? Unwholesome formations are coarse, wholesome-and-neutral formations are subtle. Wholesome-and-unwholesome formations are coarse, neutral formations are subtle. Formations joined with painful feeling are coarse, formations joined with pleasant and neutral feeling are subtle. Formations joined with pleasant-and-painful feeling are coarse, formations joined with neutral feeling are subtle. The formations of one not in an attainment are coarse, the formations of one in an attainment are subtle. Formations with mental taints are coarse, formations free of mental taints are subtle. But formations should also be seen as coarse or subtle only in comparison with these or those other formations. ^2-23

24. Herein, what are inferior formations, what are superior formations? Unwholesome formations are inferior, wholesome-and-neutral formations are superior. Wholesome-and-unwholesome formations are inferior, neutral formations are superior. Formations joined with painful feeling are inferior, formations joined with pleasant and neutral feeling are superior. Formations joined with pleasant-and-painful feeling are inferior, formations joined with neutral feeling are superior. The formations of one not in an attainment are inferior, the formations of one in an attainment are superior. Formations with mental taints are inferior, formations free of mental taints are superior. But formations should also be seen as inferior or superior only in comparison with these or those other formations. ^2-24

25. Herein, what are far formations? Unwholesome formations are far from wholesome-and-neutral formations; wholesome-and-neutral formations are far from unwholesome formations; wholesome formations are far from unwholesome-and-neutral formations; unwholesome-and-neutral formations are far from wholesome formations; neutral formations are far from wholesome-and-unwholesome formations; wholesome-and-unwholesome formations are far from neutral formations. Formations joined with painful feeling are far from formations joined with pleasant and neutral feeling; formations joined with pleasant and neutral feeling are far from formations joined with painful feeling; formations joined with pleasant feeling are far from formations joined with painful and neutral feeling; formations joined with painful and neutral feeling are far from formations joined with pleasant feeling; formations joined with neutral feeling are far from formations joined with pleasant-and-painful feeling; formations joined with pleasant-and-painful feeling are far from formations joined with neutral feeling. The formations of one not in an attainment are far from the formations of one in an attainment; the formations of one in an attainment are far from the formations of one not in an attainment. Formations with mental taints are far from formations free of mental taints; formations free of mental taints are far from formations with mental taints. These are called far formations.
Herein, what are near formations? Unwholesome formations are near unwholesome formations; wholesome formations are near wholesome formations; neutral formations are near neutral formations. Formations joined with painful feeling are near formations joined with painful feeling; formations joined with pleasant feeling are near formations joined with pleasant feeling; formations joined with neutral feeling are near formations joined with neutral feeling. The formations of one not in an attainment are near the formations of one not in an attainment; the formations of one in an attainment are near the formations of one in an attainment. Formations with mental taints are near formations with mental taints; formations free of mental taints are near formations free of mental taints. These are called near formations. But formations should also be seen as far or near only in comparison with these or those other formations. ^2-25

##### The Aggregate of Consciousness ^2-1-1-5-0

26. Herein, what is the aggregate of consciousness? Whatever consciousness there is — past, future, or present; internal or external; coarse or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near — all of that, gathered and grouped together as one: this is called the aggregate of consciousness. ^2-26

27. Herein, what is past consciousness? Consciousness that has ceased, disappeared, changed, gone, completely vanished — having arisen and then passed away — belonging to the past, counted as belonging to the past, namely eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, mind-consciousness: this is called past consciousness.
Herein, what is future consciousness? Consciousness that is not born, has not come to be, has not been generated, has not been produced, has not been brought into being, has not appeared, has not arisen, has not co-arisen, has not come up, has not originated, belonging to the future, counted as belonging to the future, namely eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, mind-consciousness: this is called future consciousness.
Herein, what is present consciousness? Consciousness that is born, has come to be, has been generated, has been produced, has been brought into being, has appeared, has arisen, has co-arisen, has come up, has originated, belonging to the present, counted as belonging to the present, namely eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, mind-consciousness: this is called present consciousness. ^2-27

28. Herein, what is internal consciousness? Consciousness belonging internally, individually, exclusively, and personally, to this or that being — namely eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, mind-consciousness: this is called internal consciousness.
Herein, what is external consciousness? Consciousness belonging internally, individually, exclusively, and personally, to this or that other being or other person — namely eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, mind-consciousness: this is called external consciousness. ^2-28

29. Herein, what is coarse consciousness, what is subtle consciousness? Unwholesome consciousness is coarse, wholesome-and-neutral consciousness is subtle. Wholesome-and-unwholesome consciousness is coarse, neutral consciousness is subtle. Consciousness joined with painful feeling is coarse, consciousness joined with pleasant and neutral feeling is subtle. Consciousness joined with pleasant-and-painful feeling is coarse, consciousness joined with neutral feeling is subtle. The consciousness of one not in an attainment is coarse, the consciousness of one in an attainment is subtle. Consciousness with mental taints is coarse, consciousness free of mental taints is subtle. But consciousness should also be seen as coarse or subtle only in comparison with this or that other consciousness. ^2-29

30. Herein, what is inferior consciousness, what is superior consciousness? Unwholesome consciousness is inferior, wholesome-and-neutral consciousness is superior. Wholesome-and-unwholesome consciousness is inferior, neutral consciousness is superior. Consciousness joined with painful feeling is inferior, consciousness joined with pleasant and neutral feeling is superior. Consciousness joined with pleasant-and-painful feeling is inferior, consciousness joined with neutral feeling is superior. The consciousness of one not in an attainment is inferior, the consciousness of one in an attainment is superior. Consciousness with mental taints is inferior, consciousness free of mental taints is superior. 31. Herein, what is far consciousness? Unwholesome consciousness is far from wholesome-and-neutral consciousness; wholesome-and-neutral consciousness is far from unwholesome consciousness; wholesome consciousness is far from unwholesome-and-neutral consciousness; unwholesome-and-neutral consciousness is far from wholesome consciousness; neutral consciousness is far from wholesome-and-unwholesome consciousness; wholesome-and-unwholesome consciousness is far from neutral consciousness. Consciousness joined with painful feeling is far from consciousness joined with pleasant and neutral feeling; consciousness joined with pleasant and neutral feeling is far from consciousness joined with painful feeling; consciousness joined with pleasant feeling is far from consciousness joined with painful and neutral feeling; consciousness joined with painful and neutral feeling is far from consciousness joined with pleasant feeling; consciousness joined with neutral feeling is far from consciousness joined with pleasant-and-painful feeling; consciousness joined with pleasant-and-painful feeling is far from consciousness joined with neutral feeling. The consciousness of one not in an attainment is far from the consciousness of one in an attainment; the consciousness of one in an attainment is far from the consciousness of one not in an attainment. Consciousness with mental taints is far from consciousness free of mental taints; consciousness free of mental taints is far from consciousness with mental taints: this is called far consciousness.
Herein, what is near consciousness? Unwholesome consciousness is near unwholesome consciousness; wholesome consciousness is near wholesome consciousness; neutral consciousness is near neutral consciousness. Consciousness joined with painful feeling is near consciousness joined with painful feeling; consciousness joined with pleasant feeling is near consciousness joined with pleasant feeling; consciousness joined with neutral feeling is near consciousness joined with neutral feeling. The consciousness of one not in an attainment is near the consciousness of one not in an attainment; the consciousness of one in an attainment is near the consciousness of one in an attainment. Consciousness with mental taints is near consciousness with mental taints; consciousness free of mental taints is near consciousness free of mental taints: this is called near consciousness. But consciousness should also be seen as far or near only in comparison with this or that other consciousness.
Discourse Classification. ^2-31

#### Abhidhamma Classification ^2-1-2-0

32. The five aggregates: the aggregate of material form, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations, the aggregate of consciousness. ^2-32

##### The Aggregate of Material Form ^2-1-2-1-0

33. Herein, what is the aggregate of material form? As one kind, the aggregate of material form is: all material form is not a root, rootless, dissociated from a root, with conditions, conditioned, material form, worldly, subject to mental taints, bound by a fetter, tied, swept by a flood, yoked, subject to hindrance, wrongly grasped, able to be clung to, open to defilement, neutral, without an object, not a mental factor, dissociated from mind, neither a result nor something that produces a result, not defiled but open to defilement, without applied and sustained thought, not merely with sustained thought alone, without applied thought and without sustained thought, not accompanied by joy, not accompanied by happiness, not accompanied by equanimity, to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development, not rooted in what is to be abandoned by seeing or by development, neither leading to accumulation nor to dismantling, neither in training nor beyond training, limited, belonging to the sense sphere, not belonging to the fine-material sphere, not belonging to the immaterial sphere, included, not un-included, not fixed, not leading to liberation, arisen, cognizable by the six kinds of consciousness, impermanent, overcome by aging. This is how, as one kind, the aggregate of material form is described.
As two kinds, the aggregate of material form is: there is material form that is derived, and material form that is not derived. There is material form that is clung to, and material form that is not clung to. There is material form that is clung to and able to be clung to, and material form that is not clung to but able to be clung to. There is material form that is visible, and material form that is invisible. There is material form that offers resistance, and material form that does not. There is material form that is a faculty, and material form that is not a faculty. There is material form that is a great element, and material form that is not a great element. There is material form that is expression, and material form that is not expression. There is material form that originates from mind, and material form that does not. There is material form that co-arises with mind, and material form that does not. There is material form that follows mind, and material form that does not. There is material form that is internal, and material form that is external. There is material form that is coarse, and material form that is subtle. There is material form that is far, and material form that is near ... there is material form that is solid food, and material form that is not solid food. This is how, as two kinds, the aggregate of material form is described.
(As it was analyzed in the section on material form, so it should be analyzed here.)
As three kinds, the aggregate of material form is: material form that is internal is derived; material form that is external is either derived or not derived. Material form that is internal is clung to; material form that is external is either clung to or not clung to. Material form that is internal is clung to and able to be clung to; material form that is external is either clung to and able to be clung to, or not clung to but able to be clung to ... material form that is internal is not solid food; material form that is external is either solid food or not solid food. This is how, as three kinds, the aggregate of material form is described.
As four kinds, the aggregate of material form is: material form that is derived is either clung to or not clung to; material form that is not derived is either clung to or not clung to. Material form that is derived is either clung to and able to be clung to, or not clung to but able to be clung to; material form that is not derived is likewise either clung to and able to be clung to, or not clung to but able to be clung to. Material form that is derived either offers resistance or does not; material form that is not derived either offers resistance or does not. Material form that is derived is either coarse or subtle; material form that is not derived is either coarse or subtle. Material form that is derived is either far or near; material form that is not derived is either far or near ... it is seen, heard, sensed, or cognized material form. This is how, as four kinds, the aggregate of material form is described.
As five kinds, the aggregate of material form is: the earth element, the water element, the fire element, the air element, and material form that is derived. This is how, as five kinds, the aggregate of material form is described.
As six kinds, the aggregate of material form is: material form cognizable by eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, mind-consciousness. This is how, as six kinds, the aggregate of material form is described.
As seven kinds, the aggregate of material form is: material form cognizable by eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, the mind element, the mind-consciousness element. This is how, as seven kinds, the aggregate of material form is described.
As eight kinds, the aggregate of material form is: material form cognizable by eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness; material form cognizable by body-consciousness is either accompanied by a pleasant contact or accompanied by a painful contact; material form cognizable by the mind element; material form cognizable by the mind-consciousness element. This is how, as eight kinds, the aggregate of material form is described.
As nine kinds, the aggregate of material form is: the eye faculty, the ear faculty, the nose faculty, the tongue faculty, the body faculty, the faculty of femininity, the faculty of masculinity, the life faculty, and material form that is not a faculty. This is how, as nine kinds, the aggregate of material form is described.

This is how, as twenty-four kinds, the aggregate of perception is described.

##### The Aggregate of Formations ^2-1-2-4-0

92. Herein, what is the aggregate of formations? As one kind, the aggregate of formations is: joined with mind.
As two kinds, the aggregate of formations is: some is a root, some is not a root.
As three kinds, the aggregate of formations is: some is wholesome, some is unwholesome, some is neutral.
As four kinds, the aggregate of formations is: some belongs to the sense sphere, some to the fine-material sphere, some to the immaterial sphere, some is not included in any sphere.
As five kinds, the aggregate of formations is: some is joined with the faculty of pleasure, some joined with the faculty of pain, some joined with the faculty of gladness, some joined with the faculty of sadness, some joined with the faculty of equanimity. This is how, as five kinds, the aggregate of formations is described.
As six kinds, the aggregate of formations is: intention born of eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, mind-contact. This is how, as six kinds, the aggregate of formations is described.
As seven kinds, the aggregate of formations is: intention born of eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, contact via the mind element, contact via the mind-consciousness element. This is how, as seven kinds, the aggregate of formations is described.
As eight kinds, the aggregate of formations is: intention born of eye-contact ... body-contact, and this is either accompanied by happiness or accompanied by pain; intention born of contact via the mind element; intention born of contact via the mind-consciousness element. This is how, as eight kinds, the aggregate of formations is described.
As nine kinds, the aggregate of formations is: intention born of eye-contact ... contact via the mind element, contact via the mind-consciousness element, and this is either wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral. This is how, as nine kinds, the aggregate of formations is described.
As ten kinds, the aggregate of formations is: intention born of eye-contact ... body-contact, and this is either accompanied by happiness or accompanied by pain; contact via the mind element; contact via the mind-consciousness element, and this is either wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral. This is how, as ten kinds, the aggregate of formations is described. ^2-92

93. As one kind, the aggregate of formations is: joined with mind.
As two kinds, the aggregate of formations is: some is a root, some is not a root.
As three kinds, the aggregate of formations is: some is joined with pleasant feeling, some joined with painful feeling, some joined with neutral feeling. Some is a result, some produces a result, some is neither a result nor something that produces a result. Some is clung to and able to be clung to, some is not clung to but able to be clung to, some is not clung to and not able to be clung to. Some is defiled and open to defilement, some is not defiled but open to defilement, some is not defiled and not open to defilement. Some has applied and sustained thought, some has only sustained thought, some has neither. Some is accompanied by joy, some by happiness, some by equanimity. Some is to be abandoned by seeing, some by development, some by neither. Some is rooted in what is to be abandoned by seeing, some in what is to be abandoned by development, some in neither. Some leads to accumulation, some to dismantling, some to neither. Some is still in training, some is beyond training, some is neither. Some is limited, some is expanded, some is measureless. Some has a limited object, some has an expanded object, some has a measureless object. Some is inferior, some is middling, some is superior. Some is fixed in wrongness, some is fixed in rightness, some is not fixed. Some has the path as object, some has the path as root, some has the path as its dominant factor. Some is arisen, some is not yet arisen, some is bound to arise. Some is past, some is future, some is present. Some has a past object, some has a future object, some has a present object. Some is internal, some is external, some is both internal and external. Some has an internal object, some has an external object, some has an object that is both internal and external ... This is how, as ten kinds, the aggregate of formations is described. ^2-93

94. As one kind, the aggregate of formations is: joined with mind.
As two kinds, the aggregate of formations is: some is rooted, some is rootless. Some is joined with a root, some is dissociated from a root. Some is both a root and rooted, some is rooted but not itself a root. Some is both a root and joined with a root, some is joined with a root but not itself a root. Some is not a root but rooted, some is not a root and rootless. Some is worldly, some is beyond the world. Some is knowable by some consciousness, some is not knowable by any. Some is itself a mental taint, some is not. Some is subject to mental taints, some is free of them. Some is joined with a taint, some is dissociated from a taint. Some is both a taint and subject to taints, some is subject to taints but not itself a taint. Some is both a taint and joined with a taint, some is joined with a taint but not itself a taint. Some is dissociated from taints but still subject to them, some is dissociated from taints and free of them. Some is itself a fetter, some is not. Some is bound by a fetter, some is not. Some is joined with a fetter, some is dissociated from a fetter. Some is both a fetter and bound by a fetter, some is bound by a fetter but not itself a fetter. Some is both a fetter and joined with a fetter, some is joined with a fetter but not itself a fetter. Some is dissociated from a fetter but still bound by it, some is dissociated from a fetter and not bound by it.
Some is itself a tie, some is not. Some is tied, some is not tied. Some is joined with a tie, some is dissociated from a tie. Some is both a tie and tied, some is tied but not itself a tie. Some is both a tie and joined with a tie, some is joined with a tie but not itself a tie. Some is dissociated from a tie but still tied, some is dissociated from a tie and not tied. Some is itself a flood, some is not. Some is swept by a flood, some is not. Some is joined with a flood, some is dissociated from a flood. Some is both a flood and swept by it, some is swept by a flood but not itself a flood. Some is both a flood and joined with a flood, some is joined with a flood but not itself a flood. Some is dissociated from a flood but still swept by it, some is dissociated from a flood and not swept by it. Some is itself a yoke, some is not. Some is yoked, some is not. Some is joined with a yoke, some is dissociated from a yoke. Some is both a yoke and yoked, some is yoked but not itself a yoke. Some is both a yoke and joined with a yoke, some is joined with a yoke but not itself a yoke. Some is dissociated from a yoke but still yoked, some is dissociated from a yoke and not yoked. Some is itself a hindrance, some is not. Some is subject to hindrance, some is not. Some is joined with a hindrance, some is dissociated from a hindrance. Some is both a hindrance and subject to it, some is subject to a hindrance but not itself a hindrance. Some is both a hindrance and joined with a hindrance, some is joined with a hindrance but not itself a hindrance. Some is dissociated from a hindrance but still subject to it, some is dissociated from a hindrance and not subject to it.
Some is itself wrong grasping, some is not. Some is wrongly grasped, some is not. Some is joined with wrong grasping, some is dissociated from wrong grasping. Some is both wrong grasping and wrongly grasped, some is wrongly grasped but not itself wrong grasping. Some is dissociated from wrong grasping but still wrongly grasped, some is dissociated from wrong grasping and not wrongly grasped. Some is clung to, some is not. Some is itself clinging, some is not. Some is able to be clung to, some is not. Some is joined with clinging, some is dissociated from clinging. Some is both clinging and able to be clung to, some is able to be clung to but not itself clinging. Some is both clinging and joined with clinging, some is joined with clinging but not itself clinging. Some is dissociated from clinging but still able to be clung to, some is dissociated from clinging and not able to be clung to.
Some is itself a defilement, some is not. Some is open to defilement, some is not. Some is defiled, some is not. Some is joined with a defilement, some is dissociated from a defilement. Some is both a defilement and open to it, some is open to defilement but not itself a defilement. Some is both a defilement and defiled by it, some is defiled but not itself a defilement. Some is both a defilement and joined with a defilement, some is joined with a defilement but not itself a defilement. Some is dissociated from a defilement but still open to it, some is dissociated from a defilement and not open to it. Some is to be abandoned by seeing, some is not. Some is to be abandoned by development, some is not. Some is rooted in what is to be abandoned by seeing, some is not. Some is rooted in what is to be abandoned by development, some is not.
Some has applied thought, some lacks it. Some has sustained thought, some lacks it. Some has joy, some lacks it. Some is accompanied by joy, some is not. Some is accompanied by happiness, some is not. Some is accompanied by equanimity, some is not. Some belongs to the sense sphere, some does not. Some belongs to the fine-material sphere, some does not. Some belongs to the immaterial sphere, some does not. Some is included, some is not. Some leads to liberation, some does not. Some is fixed, some is not. Some is surpassable, some is unsurpassed. Some is conflicted, some is peaceful.
As three kinds, the aggregate of formations is: some is wholesome, some is unwholesome, some is neutral ... This is how, as ten kinds, the aggregate of formations is described. ^2-94

##### The Aggregate of Consciousness ^2-1-2-5-0

121. Herein, what is the aggregate of consciousness? As one kind, the aggregate of consciousness is: joined with contact.
As two kinds, the aggregate of consciousness is: some is rooted, some is rootless.
As three kinds, the aggregate of consciousness is: some is wholesome, some is unwholesome, some is neutral.
As four kinds, the aggregate of consciousness is: some belongs to the sense sphere, some to the fine-material sphere, some to the immaterial sphere, some is not included in any sphere.
As five kinds, the aggregate of consciousness is: some is joined with the faculty of pleasure, some joined with the faculty of pain, some joined with the faculty of gladness, some joined with the faculty of sadness, some joined with the faculty of equanimity. This is how, as five kinds, the aggregate of consciousness is described.
As six kinds, the aggregate of consciousness is: eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, mind-consciousness. This is how, as six kinds, the aggregate of consciousness is described.
As seven kinds, the aggregate of consciousness is: eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, the mind element, the mind-consciousness element. This is how, as seven kinds, the aggregate of consciousness is described.
As eight kinds, the aggregate of consciousness is: eye-consciousness ... body-consciousness, and this is either accompanied by happiness or accompanied by pain; the mind element; the mind-consciousness element. This is how, as eight kinds, the aggregate of consciousness is described.
As nine kinds, the aggregate of consciousness is: eye-consciousness ... body-consciousness, the mind element, the mind-consciousness element, and this is either wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral. This is how, as nine kinds, the aggregate of consciousness is described.
As ten kinds, the aggregate of consciousness is: eye-consciousness ... body-consciousness, and this is either accompanied by happiness or accompanied by pain; the mind element; the mind-consciousness element, and this is either wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral. This is how, as ten kinds, the aggregate of consciousness is described. ^2-121

#### Questions and Answers ^2-1-3-0

150. The five aggregates: the aggregate of material form, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations, the aggregate of consciousness. ^2-150

151. Of the five aggregates, how many are wholesome, how many unwholesome, how many neutral ... how many conflicted, how many peaceful? ^2-151

##### Triads ^2-1-3-1-0

152. The aggregate of material form is neutral. The other four aggregates may be wholesome, may be unwholesome, or may be neutral. Two aggregates should not be said to be joined with pleasant feeling, joined with painful feeling, or joined with neutral feeling. Three aggregates may be joined with pleasant feeling, may be joined with painful feeling, or may be joined with neutral feeling. The aggregate of material form is neither a result nor something that produces a result. The other four aggregates may be a result, may produce a result, or may be neither. The aggregate of material form may be clung to and able to be clung to, or may be not clung to but able to be clung to. The other four aggregates may be clung to and able to be clung to, may be not clung to but able to be clung to, or may be not clung to and not able to be clung to.
The aggregate of material form is not defiled and not open to defilement. The other four aggregates may be defiled and open to defilement, may be not defiled but open to defilement, or may be not defiled and not open to defilement. The aggregate of material form has neither applied nor sustained thought. Three aggregates may have applied and sustained thought, may have only sustained thought, or may have neither. The aggregate of formations may have applied and sustained thought, may have only sustained thought, may have neither, or should not be said to have applied and sustained thought, only sustained thought, or neither. The aggregate of material form should not be said to be accompanied by joy, accompanied by happiness, or accompanied by equanimity. The aggregate of feeling may be accompanied by joy without being accompanied by happiness or equanimity, or should not be said to be accompanied by joy. Three aggregates may be accompanied by joy, may be accompanied by happiness, or may be accompanied by equanimity, or should not be said to be accompanied by joy, accompanied by happiness, or accompanied by equanimity.
The aggregate of material form is to be abandoned by neither seeing nor development. The other four aggregates may be abandoned by seeing, may be abandoned by development, or may be abandoned by neither. The aggregate of material form is rooted in neither what is to be abandoned by seeing nor what is to be abandoned by development. The other four aggregates may be rooted in what is to be abandoned by seeing, in what is to be abandoned by development, or in neither. The aggregate of material form leads neither to accumulation nor to dismantling. The other four aggregates may lead to accumulation, may lead to dismantling, or may lead to neither. The aggregate of material form is neither in training nor beyond training. The other four aggregates may be still in training, may be beyond training, or may be neither. The aggregate of material form is limited. The other four aggregates may be limited, may be expanded, or may be measureless. The aggregate of material form has no object. The other four aggregates may have a limited object, may have an expanded object, or may have a measureless object, or should not be said to have a limited object, an expanded object, or a measureless object. The aggregate of material form is middling. The other four aggregates may be inferior, may be middling, or may be superior. The aggregate of material form is not fixed. The other four aggregates may be fixed in wrongness, may be fixed in rightness, or may be not fixed.
The aggregate of material form has no object. The other four aggregates may have the path as object, may have the path as root, may have the path as their dominant factor, or should not be said to have the path as object, as root, or as dominant factor; they may be arisen, may be not yet arisen, or may be bound to arise; they may be past, may be future, or may be present. The aggregate of material form has no object. The other four aggregates may have a past object, may have a future object, or may have a present object, or should not be said to have a past object, a future object, or a present object; they may be internal, may be external, or may be both internal and external. The other four aggregates are invisible and without resistance. The aggregate of material form may be visible and offer resistance, may be invisible but offer resistance, or may be invisible and without resistance. ^2-152

### Analysis of the Sense-Fields ^2-2-0

#### Discourse Classification ^2-2-1-0

154. The twelve sense-fields: the eye sense-field, the sight sense-field, the ear sense-field, the sense-field of sounds, the nose sense-field, the smell sense-field, the tongue sense-field, the taste sense-field, the body sense-field, the tangible sense-field, the mind sense-field, the mental-object sense-field.
The eye is impermanent, suffering, non-self, subject to change. Sights are impermanent, suffering, non-self, subject to change. The ear is impermanent, suffering, non-self, subject to change. Sounds are impermanent, suffering, non-self, subject to change. The nose is impermanent, suffering, non-self, subject to change. Smells are impermanent, suffering, non-self, subject to change. The tongue is impermanent, suffering, non-self, subject to change. Tastes are impermanent, suffering, non-self, subject to change. The body is impermanent, suffering, non-self, subject to change. Things touched are impermanent, suffering, non-self, subject to change. The mind is impermanent, suffering, non-self, subject to change. Mental objects are impermanent, suffering, non-self, subject to change.
Discourse Classification. ^2-154

#### Abhidhamma Classification ^2-2-2-0

155. The twelve sense-fields: the eye sense-field, the ear sense-field, the nose sense-field, the tongue sense-field, the body sense-field, the mind sense-field, the sight sense-field, the sense-field of sounds, the smell sense-field, the taste sense-field, the tangible sense-field, the mental-object sense-field. ^2-155

156. Herein, what is the eye sense-field? The eye that, derived from the four great elements, is a sensitive surface, included in one's own being, invisible, and offering resistance; that eye — itself invisible and offering resistance — by which one has seen, sees, will see, or may see a visible form that is visible and offers resistance: this is the eye, this is the eye sense-field, this is the eye element, this is the eye faculty; this is the world, this is the door, this is the ocean; this is the bright, this is the field, this is the ground; this is the guide, this is the leader; this is the near shore, this is the empty village. This is called "the eye sense-field". ^2-156

157. Herein, what is the ear sense-field? The ear that, derived from the four great elements, is a sensitive surface, included in one's own being, invisible, and offering resistance; that ear — itself invisible and offering resistance — by which one has heard, hears, will hear, or may hear a sound that is invisible and offers resistance: this is the ear, this is the ear sense-field, this is the ear element, this is the ear faculty; this is the world, this is the door, this is the ocean; this is the bright, this is the field, this is the ground; this is the near shore, this is the empty village. This is called "the ear sense-field". ^2-157

158. Herein, what is the nose sense-field? The nose that, derived from the four great elements, is a sensitive surface, included in one's own being, invisible, and offering resistance; that nose — itself invisible and offering resistance — by which one has smelled, smells, will smell, or may smell a smell that is invisible and offers resistance: this is the nose, this is the nose sense-field, this is the nose element, this is the nose faculty; this is the world, this is the door, this is the ocean; this is the bright, this is the field, this is the ground; this is the near shore, this is the empty village. This is called "the nose sense-field". ^2-158

159. Herein, what is the tongue sense-field? The tongue that, derived from the four great elements, is a sensitive surface, included in one's own being, invisible, and offering resistance; that tongue — itself invisible and offering resistance — by which one has tasted, tastes, will taste, or may taste a taste that is invisible and offers resistance: this is the tongue, this is the tongue sense-field, this is the tongue element, this is the tongue faculty; this is the world, this is the door, this is the ocean; this is the bright, this is the field, this is the ground; this is the near shore, this is the empty village. This is called "the tongue sense-field". ^2-159

160. Herein, what is the body sense-field? The body that, derived from the four great elements, is a sensitive surface, included in one's own being, invisible, and offering resistance; that body — itself invisible and offering resistance — by which one has touched, touches, will touch, or may touch a tangible thing that is invisible and offers resistance: this is the body, this is the body sense-field, this is the body element, this is the body faculty; this is the world, this is the door, this is the ocean; this is the bright, this is the field, this is the ground; this is the near shore, this is the empty village. This is called "the body sense-field". ^2-160

161. Herein, what is the mind sense-field? As one kind, the mind sense-field is: joined with contact.
As two kinds, the mind sense-field is: some is rooted, some is rootless.
As three kinds, the mind sense-field is: some is wholesome, some is unwholesome, some is neutral.
As four kinds, the mind sense-field is: some belongs to the sense sphere, some to the fine-material sphere, some to the immaterial sphere, some is not included in any sphere.
As five kinds, the mind sense-field is: some is joined with the faculty of pleasure, some joined with the faculty of pain, some joined with the faculty of gladness, some joined with the faculty of sadness, some joined with the faculty of equanimity.
As six kinds, the mind sense-field is: eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, mind-consciousness. This is how, as six kinds, the mind sense-field is described.
As seven kinds, the mind sense-field is: eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, the mind element, the mind-consciousness element. This is how, as seven kinds, the mind sense-field is described.
As eight kinds, the mind sense-field is: eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness that is accompanied by pleasant feeling or accompanied by painful feeling, the mind element, the mind-consciousness element. This is how, as eight kinds, the mind sense-field is described.
As nine kinds, the mind sense-field is: eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, the mind element, the mind-consciousness element that is wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral. This is how, as nine kinds, the mind sense-field is described.
As ten kinds, the mind sense-field is: eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness that is accompanied by pleasant feeling or accompanied by painful feeling, the mind element, the mind-consciousness element that is wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral. This is how, as ten kinds, the mind sense-field is described.
As one kind, the mind sense-field is: joined with contact.
As two kinds, the mind sense-field is: some is rooted, some is rootless.
As three kinds, the mind sense-field is: some is joined with pleasant feeling, some joined with painful feeling, some joined with neutral feeling... This is how, as many kinds, the mind sense-field is described. This is called "the mind sense-field". ^2-161

162. Herein, what is the sight sense-field? The sight that, derived from the four great elements, is the shining of colour, visible, and offering resistance — blue, yellow, red, white, black, crimson, greenish, the colour of a mango shoot; long, short, fine, stout; round, circular, square, six-sided, eight-sided, sixteen-sided; low-lying, highland; shade, sunshine, light, darkness; cloud, mist, smoke, dust; the shining colour of the moon's disc, the shining colour of the sun's disc, the shining colour of the stars, the shining colour of a mirror's disc, the shining colour of gems, conch shells, pearls, and cat's-eye, the shining colour of gold and silver — or whatever other sight there is, derived from the four great elements, the shining of colour, visible, and offering resistance; that sight, visible and offering resistance, which one has seen, sees, will see, or may see with the eye that is invisible and offers resistance: this is a sight, this is the sight sense-field, this is the sight element. This is called "the sight sense-field". ^2-162

163. Herein, what is the sense-field of sounds? The sound that, derived from the four great elements, is invisible and offers resistance — the sound of a drum, the sound of a small drum, the sound of a conch, the sound of a tabor, the sound of singing, the sound of music, the sound of cymbals, the sound of clapping, the cries of beings, the sound of colliding elements, the sound of wind, the sound of water, the sound of humans, the sound of non-humans — or whatever other sound there is, derived from the four great elements, invisible and offering resistance; that sound, invisible and offering resistance, which one has heard, hears, will hear, or may hear with the ear that is invisible and offers resistance: this is a sound, this is the sense-field of sounds, this is the sound element. This is called "the sense-field of sounds". ^2-163

164. Herein, what is the smell sense-field? The smell that, derived from the four great elements, is invisible and offers resistance — the smell of a root, the smell of heartwood, the smell of bark, the smell of a leaf, the smell of a flower, the smell of a fruit, the smell of something raw, a putrid smell, a fragrant smell, a foul smell — or whatever other smell there is, derived from the four great elements, invisible and offering resistance; that smell, invisible and offering resistance, which one has smelled, smells, will smell, or may smell with the nose that is invisible and offers resistance: this is a smell, this is the smell sense-field, this is the smell element. This is called "the smell sense-field". ^2-164

165. Herein, what is the taste sense-field? The taste that, derived from the four great elements, is invisible and offers resistance — the taste of a root, the taste of a stem, the taste of bark, the taste of a leaf, the taste of a flower, the taste of a fruit; sour, sweet, bitter, pungent, salty, alkaline, sharp, astringent; pleasant, unpleasant — or whatever other taste there is, derived from the four great elements, invisible and offering resistance; that taste, invisible and offering resistance, which one has tasted, tastes, will taste, or may taste with the tongue that is invisible and offers resistance: this is a taste, this is the taste sense-field, this is the taste element. This is called "the taste sense-field". ^2-165

166. Herein, what is the tangible sense-field? The earth element, the fire element, the air element; hard, soft, smooth, rough; pleasant to the touch, painful to the touch; heavy, light; that tangible thing, invisible and offering resistance, which one has touched, touches, will touch, or may touch with the body that is invisible and offers resistance: this is a tangible thing, this is the tangible sense-field, this is the tangible element. This is called "the tangible sense-field". ^2-166

167. Herein, what is the mental-object sense-field? The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations, whatever material form there is that is invisible and without resistance and included in the mental-object sense-field, and the unconditioned element.
Herein, what is the aggregate of feeling? As one kind, the aggregate of feeling is: joined with contact. As two kinds, the aggregate of feeling is: some is rooted, some is rootless. As three kinds, the aggregate of feeling is: some is wholesome, some is unwholesome, some is neutral... This is how, as ten kinds, the aggregate of feeling is described... This is how, as many kinds, the aggregate of feeling is described. This is called "the aggregate of feeling".
Herein, what is the aggregate of perception? As one kind, the aggregate of perception is: joined with contact. As two kinds, the aggregate of perception is: some is rooted, some is rootless. As three kinds, the aggregate of perception is: some is wholesome, some is unwholesome, some is neutral... This is how, as ten kinds, the aggregate of perception is described... This is how, as many kinds, the aggregate of perception is described. This is called "the aggregate of perception".
Herein, what is the aggregate of formations? As one kind, the aggregate of formations is: joined with mind. As two kinds, the aggregate of formations is: some is a root, some is not a root. As three kinds, the aggregate of formations is: some is wholesome, some is unwholesome, some is neutral... This is how, as ten kinds, the aggregate of formations is described... This is how, as many kinds, the aggregate of formations is described. This is called "the aggregate of formations".
Herein, what is the material form that is invisible, without resistance, and included in the mental-object sense-field? The faculty of femininity, the faculty of masculinity... solid food. This is called the material form that is "invisible, without resistance, and included in the mental-object sense-field".
Herein, what is the unconditioned element? The destruction of desire, the destruction of hatred, the destruction of delusion — this is called "the unconditioned element".
This is called the mental-object sense-field.
Abhidhamma Classification. ^2-167

#### Questions and Answers ^2-2-3-0

168. The twelve sense-fields: the eye sense-field, the sight sense-field, the ear sense-field, the sense-field of sounds, the nose sense-field, the smell sense-field, the tongue sense-field, the taste sense-field, the body sense-field, the tangible sense-field, the mind sense-field, the mental-object sense-field. ^2-168

169. Of the twelve sense-fields, how many are wholesome, how many unwholesome, how many neutral... how many conflicted, how many peaceful? ^2-169

##### Triads ^2-2-3-1-0

170. Ten sense-fields are neutral. Two sense-fields may be wholesome, may be unwholesome, or may be neutral. Ten sense-fields should not be said to be joined with pleasant feeling, joined with painful feeling, or joined with neutral feeling. The mind sense-field may be joined with pleasant feeling, may be joined with painful feeling, or may be joined with neutral feeling. Five sense-fields are clung to and able to be clung to. The sense-field of sounds is not clung to but able to be clung to. Four sense-fields may be clung to and able to be clung to, may be not clung to but able to be clung to, or may be not able to be clung to. Ten sense-fields neither lead to accumulation nor to dismantling. Two sense-fields may lead to accumulation, may lead to dismantling, or may lead to neither. Ten sense-fields are neither in training nor beyond training. Two sense-fields may be still in training, may be beyond training, or may be neither. Ten sense-fields are limited. Two sense-fields may be limited, may be expanded, or may be measureless. Ten sense-fields have no object. Ten sense-fields are middling. Two sense-fields may be inferior, may be middling, or may be superior. Ten sense-fields are not fixed. Two sense-fields may be fixed in wrongness, may be fixed in rightness, or may be not fixed.
Ten sense-fields have no object. Two sense-fields may have the path as object, may have the path as root, or may have the path as their dominant factor, or should not be said to have the path as object, as root, or as dominant factor. Five sense-fields may be arisen or may be bound to arise, and should not be said to be "not arisen". The mental-object sense-field may be arisen, may be not arisen, or may be bound to arise, or should not be said to be arisen, not arisen, or bound to arise. Eleven sense-fields may be past, may be future, or may be present. The mental-object sense-field may be past, may be future, or may be present, or should not be said to be past, future, or present. Ten sense-fields have no object. Two sense-fields may have a past object, may have a future object, or may have a present object, or should not be said to have a past object, a future object, or a present object; they may be internal, may be external, or may be both internal and external. Ten sense-fields have no object. Two sense-fields may have an internal object, may have an external object, or may have an object that is both internal and external, or should not be said to have an internal object, an external object, or an object both internal and external. The sight sense-field is visible and offers resistance. Nine sense-fields are invisible and offer resistance. Two sense-fields are invisible and offer no resistance. ^2-170

Eleven sense-fields are not themselves a fetter. The mental-object sense-field may itself be a fetter or may not. Ten sense-fields can be bound by a fetter. Eleven sense-fields are not themselves a tie. The mental-object sense-field may itself be a tie or may not. Ten sense-fields can be tied. Two sense-fields may be tied or may not.
