### Analysis of the Elements ^2-3-0

#### Discourse Classification ^2-3-1-0

172. The six elements: the earth element, the water element, the fire element, the air element, the space element, the consciousness element. ^2-172

173. Herein, what is the earth element? The earth element is twofold: there is the internal, there is the external. Herein, what is the internal earth element? Whatever, belonging internally and individually, is hard, of a solid nature, hardness, a state of hardness, and clung to internally — namely, head hair, body hair, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, sinews, bones, bone marrow, kidneys, heart, liver, membrane, spleen, lungs, intestines, mesentery, stomach contents, feces, or whatever else there is that, belonging internally and individually, is hard, of a solid nature, hardness, a state of hardness, and clung to internally: this is called 'the internal earth element'.
Herein, what is the external earth element? Whatever, external, is hard, of a solid nature, hardness, a state of hardness, and not clung to — namely, iron, copper, tin, lead, silver, pearl, gem, beryl, conch shell, stone, coral, silver, gold, ruby, cat's-eye, grass, wood, gravel, pebbles, earth, rock, mountain, or whatever else there is that, external, is hard, of a solid nature, hardness, a state of hardness, and not clung to: this is called 'the external earth element'. Both the internal earth element and the external earth element, gathered and grouped together as one: this is called 'the earth element'. ^2-173

174. Herein, what is the water element? The water element is twofold: there is the internal, there is the external. Herein, what is the internal water element? Whatever, belonging internally and individually, is liquid, of a watery nature, moisture, a moist state, a binding together of material form, and clung to internally — namely, bile, phlegm, pus, blood, sweat, fat, tears, grease, saliva, snot, oil-of-the-joints, urine, or whatever else there is that, belonging internally and individually, is liquid, of a watery nature, moisture, a moist state, a binding together of material form, and clung to internally: this is called 'the internal water element'.
Herein, what is the external water element? Whatever, external, is liquid, of a watery nature, moisture, a moist state, a binding together of material form, and not clung to — namely, the sap of roots, the sap of stems, the sap of bark, the sap of leaves, the sap of flowers, the sap of fruits, milk, curd, ghee, butter, oil, honey, molasses, water in the ground, or water in the sky, or whatever else there is that, external, is liquid, of a watery nature, moisture, a moist state, a binding together of material form, and not clung to: this is called 'the external water element'. Both the internal water element and the external water element, gathered and grouped together as one: this is called 'the water element'. ^2-174

175. Herein, what is the fire element? The fire element is twofold: there is the internal, there is the external. Herein, what is the internal fire element? Whatever, belonging internally and individually, is fire, of a fiery nature, warmth, a warm state, heat, a heated state, and clung to internally — namely, that by which one is warmed, that by which one ages, that by which one is consumed with fever, and that by which what is eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted is properly digested, or whatever else there is that, belonging internally and individually, is fire, of a fiery nature, warmth, a warm state, heat, a heated state, and clung to internally: this is called 'the internal fire element'.
Herein, what is the external fire element? Whatever, external, is fire, of a fiery nature, warmth, a warm state, heat, a heated state, and not clung to — namely, fire from wood, fire from straw, fire from grass, fire from cow-dung, fire from husks, fire from rubbish, fire from a thunderbolt, the heat of fire, the heat of the sun, the heat of a heap of wood, the heat of a heap of grass, the heat of a heap of grain, the heat of a heap of goods, or whatever else there is that, external, is fire, of a fiery nature, warmth, a warm state, heat, a heated state, and not clung to: this is called 'the external fire element'. Both the internal fire element and the external fire element, gathered and grouped together as one: this is called 'the fire element'. ^2-175

176. Herein, what is the air element? The air element is twofold: there is the internal, there is the external. Herein, what is the internal air element? Whatever, belonging internally and individually, is air, of an airy nature, a rigidity of material form, and clung to internally — namely, upward-moving winds, downward-moving winds, winds in the belly, winds in the bowels, winds that course through the limbs, winds that feel like knife-cuts, winds that feel like razor-cuts, winds that feel like a piercing, in-breath and out-breath, or whatever else there is that, belonging internally and individually, is air, of an airy nature, a rigidity of material form, and clung to internally: this is called 'the internal air element'.
Herein, what is the external air element? Whatever, external, is air, of an airy nature, a rigidity of material form, and not clung to — namely, easterly winds, westerly winds, northerly winds, southerly winds, dusty winds, dustless winds, cold winds, hot winds, gentle winds, strong winds, storm winds, whirlwinds, winds from wings, winds from a garuda bird, winds from a palm-leaf fan, winds from a hand-fan, or whatever else there is that, external, is air, of an airy nature, a rigidity of material form, and not clung to: this is called 'the external air element'. Both the internal air element and the external air element, gathered and grouped together as one: this is called 'the air element'. ^2-176

177. Herein, what is the space element? The space element is twofold: there is the internal, there is the external. Herein, what is the internal space element? Whatever, belonging internally and individually, is space, of a spatial nature, an empty space, a state of emptiness, an opening, a state of being an opening, not touched by flesh and blood, and clung to internally — namely, the hole of the ear, the hole of the nose, the door of the mouth, that by which what is eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted is swallowed, that in which what is eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted comes to rest, and that by which what is eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted passes out from below, or whatever else there is that, belonging internally and individually, is space, of a spatial nature, an empty space, a state of emptiness, an opening, a state of being an opening, not touched by flesh and blood, and clung to internally: this is called 'the internal space element'.
Herein, what is the external space element? Whatever, external, is space, of a spatial nature, an empty space, a state of emptiness, an opening, a state of being an opening, not touched by the four great elements, and not clung to: this is called 'the external space element'. Both the internal space element and the external space element, gathered and grouped together as one: this is called 'the space element'. ^2-177

178. Herein, what is the consciousness element? The eye-consciousness element, the ear-consciousness element, the nose-consciousness element, the tongue-consciousness element, the body-consciousness element, the mind-consciousness element: this is called 'the consciousness element'.
These are the six elements. ^2-178

179. Another six elements: the pleasure element, the pain element, the gladness element, the sadness element, the equanimity element, the ignorance element. ^2-179

180. Herein, what is the pleasure element? Whatever is bodily ease, bodily pleasure, the pleasant, pleasurable feeling born of bodily contact, the pleasant, pleasurable feeling that is felt and is born of bodily contact: this is called 'the pleasure element'.
Herein, what is the pain element? Whatever is bodily discomfort, bodily pain, the unpleasant, painful feeling born of bodily contact, the unpleasant, painful feeling that is felt and is born of bodily contact: this is called 'the pain element'.
Herein, what is the gladness element? Whatever is mental ease, mental pleasure, the pleasant, pleasurable feeling born of mental contact, the pleasant, pleasurable feeling that is felt and is born of mental contact: this is called 'the gladness element'.
Herein, what is the sadness element? Whatever is mental discomfort, mental pain, the unpleasant, painful feeling born of mental contact, the unpleasant, painful feeling that is felt and is born of mental contact: this is called 'the sadness element'.
Herein, what is the equanimity element? Whatever is mental, neither ease nor discomfort, the neutral feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant, born of mental contact, felt and born of mental contact: this is called 'the equanimity element'.
Herein, what is the ignorance element? Whatever is not-knowing, not-seeing, non-penetration, non-understanding, non-awakening, non-realization, failure to grasp, failure to fully grasp, failure to examine, failure to reflect, an act done without direct seeing, dullness of mind, foolishness, lack of clear comprehension, delusion, great delusion, complete delusion, ignorance, the flood of ignorance, the yoke of ignorance, the underlying tendency of ignorance, the obsession of ignorance, the bolt of ignorance, delusion, the root of the unwholesome: this is called 'the ignorance element'.
These are the six elements. ^2-180

181. Another six elements: the sense-pleasure element, the element of ill will, the element of cruelty, the element of renunciation, the element of goodwill, the element of harmlessness. ^2-181

182. Herein, what is the sense-pleasure element? Thinking, thought, intention connected with sense-pleasure, fixing, focusing, the directing of the mind, wrong intention: this is called the sense-pleasure element. Taking the Avīci hell as the lower limit and the Paranimmitavasavatti gods as the upper limit, whatever aggregates, elements, sense-fields, material form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness belong there, are included there, within that range: this is called 'the sense-pleasure element'.
Herein, what is the element of ill will? Thinking, thought... wrong intention connected with ill will: this is called 'the element of ill will'. Or, with regard to the ten grounds for resentment, resentment of mind, aversion, irritation, opposition, anger, being angered, being greatly angered, hatred, hostility, great hostility, malice of mind, ill will of mind, wrath, becoming wrathful, the state of being wrathful, hatred, becoming hateful, the state of being hateful, malice, becoming malicious, opposition, hostility, fury, ferocity, and displeasure of mind: this is called 'the element of ill will'.
Herein, what is the element of cruelty? Thinking, thought... wrong intention connected with cruelty: this is called 'the element of cruelty'. Herein, someone harms beings with the hand, with a clod, with a stick, with a weapon, with a rope, or by some other means; whatever such harming, harassing, injuring, cruelty, hurting, offending, and injuring of others there is: this is called 'the element of cruelty'.
Herein, what is the element of renunciation? Thinking, thought... right intention connected with renunciation: this is called 'the element of renunciation'. All wholesome states, too, are 'the element of renunciation'.
Herein, what is the element of goodwill? Thinking, thought... right intention connected with goodwill: this is called 'the element of goodwill'. Whatever loving-kindness there is toward beings, the practice of loving-kindness, the state of practicing loving-kindness, the mind's release through loving-kindness: this is called 'the element of goodwill'.
Herein, what is the element of harmlessness? Thinking, thought, intention, fixing, focusing, the directing of the mind, right intention connected with harmlessness: this is called 'the element of harmlessness'. Whatever compassion there is toward beings, the practice of compassion, the state of practicing compassion, the mind's release through compassion: this is called 'the element of harmlessness'.
These are the six elements.
Thus these three sets of six, gathered and grouped together as one, make eighteen elements.
Discourse Classification. ^2-182

#### Abhidhamma Classification ^2-3-2-0

183. The eighteen elements: the eye element, the sight element, the eye-consciousness element, the ear element, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, the nose element, the smell element, the nose-consciousness element, the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, the body element, the tangible element, the body-consciousness element, the mind element, the mental-object element, the mind-consciousness element. ^2-183

184. Herein, what is the eye element? The eye that, derived from the four great elements, is a sensitive surface... this is the empty village. This is called 'the eye element'.
Herein, what is the sight element? Whatever sight there is, derived from the four great elements, the shining of colour... this is the sight element. This is called 'the sight element'.
Herein, what is the eye-consciousness element? In dependence on the eye and sights, there arises consciousness, mind, mental activity, heart, the bright, mind, the mind sense-field, the mind faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, the corresponding eye-consciousness element: this is called 'the eye-consciousness element'.
Herein, what is the ear element? The ear that, derived from the four great elements, is a sensitive surface... this is the empty village. This is called 'the ear element'.
Herein, what is the sound element? Whatever sound there is, derived from the four great elements, invisible and offering resistance... this is the sound element. This is called 'the sound element'.
Herein, what is the ear-consciousness element? In dependence on the ear and sounds, there arises consciousness, mind, mental activity, heart, the bright, mind, the mind sense-field, the mind faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, the corresponding ear-consciousness element: this is called 'the ear-consciousness element'.
Herein, what is the nose element? The nose that, derived from the four great elements, is a sensitive surface... this is the empty village. This is called 'the nose element'.
Herein, what is the smell element? Whatever smell there is, derived from the four great elements, invisible and offering resistance... this is the smell element. This is called 'the smell element'.
Herein, what is the nose-consciousness element? In dependence on the nose and smells, there arises consciousness, mind, mental activity, heart, the bright, mind, the mind sense-field, the mind faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, the corresponding nose-consciousness element: this is called 'the nose-consciousness element'.
Herein, what is the tongue element? The tongue that, derived from the four great elements, is a sensitive surface... this is the empty village. This is called 'the tongue element'.
Herein, what is the taste element? Whatever taste there is, derived from the four great elements, invisible and offering resistance... this is the taste element. This is called 'the taste element'.
Herein, what is the tongue-consciousness element? In dependence on the tongue and tastes, there arises consciousness, mind, mental activity, heart, the bright, mind, the mind sense-field, the mind faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, the corresponding tongue-consciousness element: this is called 'the tongue-consciousness element'.
Herein, what is the body element? The body that, derived from the four great elements, is a sensitive surface... this is the empty village. This is called 'the body element'.
Herein, what is the tangible element? The earth element... this is the tangible element. This is called 'the tangible element'.
Herein, what is the body-consciousness element? In dependence on the body and tangible things, there arises consciousness, mind, mental activity, heart, the bright, mind, the mind sense-field, the mind faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, the corresponding body-consciousness element: this is called 'the body-consciousness element'.
Herein, what is the mind element? Immediately after the eye-consciousness element has arisen and ceased, there arises consciousness, mind, mental activity, heart, the bright, mind, the mind sense-field, the mind faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, the corresponding mind element; immediately after the ear-consciousness element... the nose-consciousness element... the tongue-consciousness element... the body-consciousness element has arisen and ceased, there arises consciousness, mind, mental activity, heart, the bright, mind, the mind sense-field, the mind faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, the corresponding mind element; or again, with regard to all things, the first turning of attention arises as consciousness, mind, mental activity, heart, the bright, mind, the mind sense-field, the mind faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, the corresponding mind element: this is called 'the mind element'.
Herein, what is the mental-object element? The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations, whatever material form there is that is invisible and without resistance and included in the mental-object sense-field, and the unconditioned element.
Herein, what is the aggregate of feeling? As one kind, the aggregate of feeling is: joined with contact. As two kinds, the aggregate of feeling is: some is rooted, some is rootless. As three kinds, the aggregate of feeling is: some is wholesome, some is unwholesome, some is neutral... This is how, as ten kinds, the aggregate of feeling is described... This is how, as many kinds, the aggregate of feeling is described. This is called 'the aggregate of feeling'.
Herein, what is the aggregate of perception? As one kind, the aggregate of perception is: joined with contact. As two kinds, the aggregate of perception is: some is rooted, some is rootless. As three kinds, the aggregate of perception is: some is wholesome, some is unwholesome, some is neutral... This is how, as ten kinds, the aggregate of perception is described... This is how, as many kinds, the aggregate of perception is described. This is called 'the aggregate of perception'.
Herein, what is the aggregate of formations? As one kind, the aggregate of formations is: joined with mind. As two kinds, the aggregate of formations is: some is a root, some is not a root. As three kinds, the aggregate of formations is: some is wholesome, some is unwholesome, some is neutral... This is how, as ten kinds, the aggregate of formations is described... This is how, as many kinds, the aggregate of formations is described. This is called 'the aggregate of formations'.
Herein, what is the material form that is invisible, without resistance, and included in the mental-object sense-field? The faculty of femininity... solid food. This is called the material form that is 'invisible, without resistance, and included in the mental-object sense-field'.
Herein, what is the unconditioned element? The destruction of desire, the destruction of hatred, the destruction of delusion: this is called 'the unconditioned element'. This is called 'the mental-object element'.
Herein, what is the mind-consciousness element? Immediately after the eye-consciousness element has arisen and ceased, the mind element arises; immediately after the mind element has arisen and ceased, there arises consciousness, mind, mental activity... the corresponding mind-consciousness element; immediately after the ear-consciousness element... the nose-consciousness element... the tongue-consciousness element... the body-consciousness element has arisen and ceased, the mind element arises; immediately after the mind element, too, has arisen and ceased, there arises consciousness, mind, mental activity... the corresponding mind-consciousness element; or, in dependence on the mind and mental objects, there arises consciousness, mind, mental activity, heart, the bright, mind, the mind sense-field, the mind faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, the corresponding mind-consciousness element: this is called 'the mind-consciousness element'.
Abhidhamma Classification. ^2-184

The eighteen elements: the eye element, the sight element, the eye-consciousness element, the ear element, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element, the nose element, the smell element, the nose-consciousness element, the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element, the body element, the tangible element, the body-consciousness element, the mind element, the mental-object element, the mind-consciousness element.

187. Sixteen elements are neutral. Two elements may be wholesome, may be unwholesome, or may be neutral. Ten elements should not be said to be joined with pleasant feeling, joined with painful feeling, or joined with neutral feeling. Five elements are joined with neutral feeling. The body-consciousness element may be joined with pleasant feeling, may be joined with painful feeling. The mind-consciousness element may be joined with pleasant feeling, may be joined with painful feeling, or may be joined with neutral feeling. The mental-object element may be joined with pleasant feeling, may be joined with painful feeling, or may be joined with neutral feeling, or should not be said to be joined with pleasant feeling, joined with painful feeling, or joined with neutral feeling.
Ten elements are neither a result nor something that produces a result. Five elements are a result. The mind element may be a result, or may be neither a result nor something that produces a result. Two elements may be a result, may produce a result, or may be neither a result nor something that produces a result.
Ten elements are clung to and able to be clung to. The sound element is not clung to but able to be clung to. Five elements may be clung to and able to be clung to, or may be not clung to but able to be clung to. Two elements may be clung to and able to be clung to, may be not clung to but able to be clung to, or may be not clung to and not able to be clung to.
Sixteen elements are not defiled but open to defilement. The mental-object element may have applied and sustained thought, may have only sustained thought, may have neither, or should not be said to have applied and sustained thought, only sustained thought, or neither. Ten elements should not be said to be accompanied by joy, accompanied by happiness, or accompanied by equanimity. Five elements are accompanied by equanimity. Seventeen elements may be past, may be future, or may be present. The mental-object element may be past, may be future, or may be present, or should not be said to be past, future, or present. Ten elements have no object. Six elements have a present object. Two elements may be rooted in what is to be abandoned by development or may not be rooted in what is to be abandoned by development.
Fifteen elements lack applied thought. The mind element has applied thought. Two elements may have applied thought or may lack applied thought. Fifteen elements lack sustained thought. The mind element has sustained thought. Two elements may have sustained thought or may lack sustained thought. Sixteen elements lack joy. Two elements may have joy or may lack joy. Three elements may be accompanied by happiness or may not be accompanied by happiness. Eleven elements are not accompanied by equanimity. Five elements are accompanied by equanimity. ### Analysis of the Truths ^2-4-0

#### Discourse Classification ^2-4-1-0

189. The four noble truths: the noble truth of suffering, the noble truth of the origin of suffering, the noble truth of the cessation of suffering, the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering. ^2-189

##### The Truth of Suffering ^2-4-1-1-0

190. Herein, what is the noble truth of suffering? Birth is suffering, aging is suffering, death is suffering; sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are suffering; association with what is unpleasant is suffering, separation from what is pleasant is suffering, not getting what one wants is also suffering; in brief, the five aggregates affected by clinging are suffering. ^2-190

191. Herein, what is birth? Whatever, in this or that group of beings, is the birth, coming-to-birth, descent into the womb, production, appearance of the aggregates, and obtaining of the sense-fields of those beings: this is called 'birth'. ^2-191

192. Herein, what is aging? Whatever, in this or that group of beings, is the aging, decrepitude, broken teeth, grey hair, wrinkled skin, decline of vitality, and deterioration of the faculties of those beings: this is called 'aging'. ^2-192

193. Herein, what is death? Whatever, from this or that group of beings, is the falling away, passing, breaking up, disappearance, dying, death, completion of time, breaking up of the aggregates, laying down of the body, and cutting off of the life faculty of those beings: this is called 'death'. ^2-193

194. Herein, what is sorrow? For one who is touched by the loss of relatives, or by the loss of wealth, or by the loss through illness, or by the loss of virtue, or by the loss of view, or who is affected by any other kind of loss, or touched by any other kind of painful thing — the sorrow, sorrowing, state of sorrowing, inner sorrow, inner deep sorrow, burning of the heart, grief, and dart of sorrow of such a person: this is called 'sorrow'. ^2-194

195. Herein, what is lamentation? For one who is touched by the loss of relatives, or by the loss of wealth, or by the loss through illness, or by the loss of virtue, or by the loss of view, or who is affected by any other kind of loss, or touched by any other kind of painful thing — the wailing, lamenting, state of wailing, state of lamenting, weeping, wailing aloud, crying out, moaning, and state of moaning of such a person: this is called 'lamentation'. ^2-195

196. Herein, what is pain? Whatever bodily discomfort, bodily pain, the unpleasant, painful feeling born of bodily contact, the unpleasant, painful feeling that is felt and is born of bodily contact: this is called 'pain'. ^2-196

197. Herein, what is grief? Whatever mental discomfort, mental pain, the unpleasant, painful feeling born of mental contact, the unpleasant, painful feeling that is felt and is born of mental contact: this is called 'grief'. ^2-197

198. Herein, what is despair? For one who is touched by the loss of relatives, or by the loss of wealth, or by the loss through illness, or by the loss of virtue, or by the loss of view, or who is affected by any other kind of loss, or touched by any other kind of painful thing — the despair, deep despair, state of despair, and state of deep despair of such a person: this is called 'despair'. ^2-198

199. Herein, what is association with what is unpleasant, which is suffering? Here, whatever sights, sounds, smells, tastes, or tangibles are undesirable, unwanted, or displeasing to someone; or whoever wishes them harm, wishes them misfortune, wishes them discomfort, or wishes them no safety from bondage — the meeting, encountering, joining, or coming together with these: this is called 'association with what is unpleasant, which is suffering'. ^2-199

200. Herein, what is separation from what is pleasant, which is suffering? Here, whatever sights, sounds, smells, tastes, or tangibles are desirable, wanted, or pleasing to someone; or whoever wishes them good, wishes them benefit, wishes them comfort, or wishes them safety from bondage — mother, father, brother, sister, friends, colleagues, or blood relatives — the not meeting, not encountering, not joining, or not coming together with these: this is called 'separation from what is pleasant, which is suffering'. ^2-200

201. Herein, what is meant by 'not getting what one wants is also suffering'? For beings subject to birth, a wish arises like this: "Oh, that we were not subject to birth! And that birth would not come to us!" But this cannot be attained by wishing. This too is 'not getting what one wants is also suffering'.
For beings subject to aging... for beings subject to sickness... for beings subject to death... for beings subject to sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, a wish arises like this: "Oh, that we were not subject to sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair! And that sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair would not come to us!" But this cannot be attained by wishing. This too is 'not getting what one wants is also suffering'. ^2-201

202. Herein, what are, in brief, the five aggregates affected by clinging, which are suffering? They are: the aggregate of material form affected by clinging, the aggregate of feeling affected by clinging, the aggregate of perception affected by clinging, the aggregate of formations affected by clinging, the aggregate of consciousness affected by clinging. These are called, in brief, 'the five aggregates affected by clinging, which are suffering'.
This is called 'the noble truth of suffering'. ^2-202

##### The Truth of the Origin ^2-4-1-2-0

203. Herein, what is the noble truth of the origin of suffering? It is this craving that leads to renewed existence, accompanied by delight and lust, seeking delight now here, now there — namely, craving for sense pleasures, craving for existence, craving for non-existence.
Now, where does this craving arise when it arises, where does it settle when it settles? Whatever in the world is pleasant and agreeable — it is here that this craving arises when it arises, and here that it settles when it settles.
And what, in the world, is pleasant and agreeable? The eye, in the world, is pleasant and agreeable. It is here that this craving arises when it arises, and here that it settles when it settles. The ear, in the world... the nose... the tongue... the body... the mind, in the world, is pleasant and agreeable. It is here that this craving arises when it arises, and here that it settles when it settles.
Sights, in the world, are pleasant and agreeable. It is here that this craving arises when it arises, and here that it settles when it settles. Sounds, in the world... smells... tastes... tangibles... mental objects, in the world, are pleasant and agreeable. It is here that this craving arises when it arises, and here that it settles when it settles.
Eye-consciousness, in the world, is pleasant and agreeable. It is here that this craving arises when it arises, and here that it settles when it settles. Ear-consciousness, in the world... nose-consciousness... tongue-consciousness... body-consciousness... mind-consciousness, in the world, is pleasant and agreeable. It is here that this craving arises when it arises, and here that it settles when it settles.
Eye-contact, in the world, is pleasant and agreeable. It is here that this craving arises when it arises, and here that it settles when it settles. Ear-contact, in the world... nose-contact... tongue-contact... body-contact... mind-contact, in the world, is pleasant and agreeable. It is here that this craving arises when it arises, and here that it settles when it settles.
Feeling born of eye-contact, in the world, is pleasant and agreeable. It is here that this craving arises when it arises, and here that it settles when it settles. Feeling born of ear-contact, in the world... feeling born of nose-contact... feeling born of tongue-contact... feeling born of body-contact... feeling born of mind-contact, in the world, is pleasant and agreeable. It is here that this craving arises when it arises, and here that it settles when it settles.
Perception of sights, in the world, is pleasant and agreeable. It is here that this craving arises when it arises, and here that it settles when it settles. Perception of sounds, in the world... perception of smells... perception of tastes... perception of tangibles... perception of mental objects, in the world, is pleasant and agreeable. It is here that this craving arises when it arises, and here that it settles when it settles.
Volition regarding sights, in the world, is pleasant and agreeable. It is here that this craving arises when it arises, and here that it settles when it settles. It is here that this craving arises when it arises, and here that it settles when it settles.
Craving for sights, in the world, is pleasant and agreeable. It is here that this craving arises when it arises, and here that it settles when it settles. Craving for sounds, in the world... craving for smells... craving for tastes... craving for tangibles... craving for mental objects, in the world, is pleasant and agreeable. It is here that this craving arises when it arises, and here that it settles when it settles.
Thinking about sights, in the world, is pleasant and agreeable. It is here that this craving arises when it arises, and here that it settles when it settles. Thinking about sounds, in the world... thinking about smells... thinking about tastes... thinking about tangibles... thinking about mental objects, in the world, is pleasant and agreeable. It is here that this craving arises when it arises, and here that it settles when it settles.
Reflecting on sights, in the world, is pleasant and agreeable. It is here that this craving arises when it arises, and here that it settles when it settles. Reflecting on sounds, in the world, is pleasant and agreeable. It is here that this craving arises when it arises, and here that it settles when it settles. Reflecting on smells, in the world, is pleasant and agreeable. It is here that this craving arises when it arises, and here that it settles when it settles. Reflecting on tastes, in the world, is pleasant and agreeable. It is here that this craving arises when it arises, and here that it settles when it settles. Reflecting on tangibles, in the world, is pleasant and agreeable. It is here that this craving arises when it arises, and here that it settles when it settles. Reflecting on mental objects, in the world, is pleasant and agreeable. It is here that this craving arises when it arises, and here that it settles when it settles.
This is called 'the noble truth of the origin of suffering'. ^2-203

##### The Truth of Cessation ^2-4-1-3-0

204. Herein, what is the noble truth of the cessation of suffering? It is the complete fading away and cessation of that same craving, the giving up of it, the relinquishing of it, freedom from it, non-reliance on it.
Now, where is this craving abandoned when it is abandoned, where does it cease when it ceases? Whatever in the world is pleasant and agreeable — it is here that this craving is abandoned when it is abandoned, and here that it ceases when it ceases.
And what, in the world, is pleasant and agreeable? The eye, in the world, is pleasant and agreeable. It is here that this craving is abandoned when it is abandoned, and here that it ceases when it ceases. The ear, in the world... the nose... the tongue... the body... the mind, in the world, is pleasant and agreeable. It is here that this craving is abandoned when it is abandoned, and here that it ceases when it ceases.

Perception of sights, in the world... perception of sounds... perception of smells... perception of tastes... perception of tangibles... perception of mental objects, in the world, is pleasant and agreeable. It is here that this craving is abandoned when it is abandoned, and here that it ceases when it ceases.
Volition regarding sights, in the world... volition regarding sounds... volition regarding smells... volition regarding tastes... volition regarding tangibles... volition regarding mental objects, in the world, is pleasant and agreeable. Craving for sights, in the world... craving for sounds... craving for smells... craving for tastes... craving for tangibles... craving for mental objects, in the world, is pleasant and agreeable. It is here that this craving is abandoned when it is abandoned, and here that it ceases when it ceases.
Thinking about sights, in the world... thinking about sounds... thinking about smells... thinking about tastes... thinking about tangibles... thinking about mental objects, in the world, is pleasant and agreeable. It is here that this craving is abandoned when it is abandoned, and here that it ceases when it ceases.
Reflecting on sights, in the world... reflecting on sounds... reflecting on smells... reflecting on tastes... reflecting on tangibles... reflecting on mental objects, in the world, is pleasant and agreeable. It is here that this craving is abandoned when it is abandoned, and here that it ceases when it ceases.
This is called 'the noble truth of the cessation of suffering'. ^2-204

##### The Truth of the Path ^2-4-1-4-0

205. Herein, what is the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering? It is just this noble eightfold path — namely, right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration.
Herein, what is right view? Knowledge of suffering, knowledge of the origin of suffering, knowledge of the cessation of suffering, knowledge of the path leading to the cessation of suffering: this is called 'right view'.
Herein, what is right intention? The intention of renunciation, the intention of non-ill-will, the intention of harmlessness: this is called 'right intention'.
Herein, what is right speech? Abstaining from false speech, abstaining from divisive speech, abstaining from harsh speech, abstaining from idle talk: this is called 'right speech'.
Herein, what is right action? Abstaining from killing living beings, abstaining from taking what is not given, abstaining from sexual misconduct: this is called 'right action'.
Herein, what is right livelihood? Here, a noble disciple, having given up wrong livelihood, earns a living by right livelihood: this is called 'right livelihood'.
Herein, what is right effort? Here, a monk generates desire, makes an effort, arouses energy, exerts the mind, and strives for the non-arising of unarisen bad, unwholesome states. He generates desire, makes an effort, arouses energy, exerts the mind, and strives for the abandoning of arisen bad, unwholesome states. He generates desire, makes an effort, arouses energy, exerts the mind, and strives for the arising of unarisen wholesome states. He generates desire, makes an effort, arouses energy, exerts the mind, and strives for the continuation, non-confusion, increase, growth, and fulfillment by development of arisen wholesome states. This is called 'right effort'.
Herein, what is right mindfulness? Here, a monk dwells contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and grief regarding the world. He dwells contemplating feelings in feelings... mind in mind... and dwells contemplating mental objects in mental objects, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and grief regarding the world. This is called 'right mindfulness'.
Herein, what is right concentration? Here, a monk, quite secluded from sense pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the first absorption, which is accompanied by thinking and reflecting, and has joy and happiness born of seclusion. With the stilling of thinking and reflecting, he enters and dwells in the second absorption, which has inner clarity and unification of mind, is without thinking and without reflecting, and has joy and happiness born of concentration. With the fading away of joy, he dwells equanimous, mindful, and clearly comprehending, and experiences happiness with the body — that state which the noble ones describe as "one who is equanimous and mindful dwells happily" — he enters and dwells in the third absorption. With the abandoning of happiness and the abandoning of pain, with the previous disappearance of gladness and grief, he enters and dwells in the fourth absorption, which has neither pain nor pleasure and is purified by equanimity and mindfulness. This is called 'right concentration'.
This is called 'the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering'.
Discourse Classification. ^2-205

#### Abhidhamma Classification ^2-4-2-0

206. The four truths: suffering, the origin of suffering, the cessation of suffering, the path leading to the cessation of suffering.
Herein, what is the origin of suffering? Craving: this is called 'the origin of suffering'.
Herein, what is suffering? The remaining defilements; the remaining unwholesome states; the three wholesome roots that are subject to mental taints; the remaining wholesome states that are subject to mental taints; the results, subject to mental taints, of wholesome and unwholesome states; those states that are merely functional, being neither wholesome nor unwholesome nor the result of action; and all material form: this is called 'suffering'.
Herein, what is the cessation of suffering? The abandoning of craving: this is called 'the cessation of suffering'.
Herein, what is the path leading to the cessation of suffering? Here, at the time when a monk develops the world-transcending absorption that leads out of the world and leads to the dismantling of accumulation, for the abandoning of wrong views and for reaching the first stage — quite secluded from sense pleasures... he enters and dwells in the first absorption, a difficult practice with slow direct knowledge — at that time the eightfold path is present: right view... right concentration.
Herein, what is right view? The wisdom, understanding... non-delusion, investigation of states, right view, the enlightenment factor of investigation of states, a path factor, included in the path: this is called 'right view'.
Herein, what is right intention? The thinking, thought... right intention, a path factor, included in the path: this is called 'right intention'.
Herein, what is right speech? The abstaining, avoiding, refraining, abstention from the four kinds of verbal misconduct — the not doing, not committing, not transgressing the boundary, cutting off the bridge to it — right speech, a path factor, included in the path: this is called 'right speech'.
Herein, what is right action? The abstaining, avoiding, refraining, abstention from the three kinds of bodily misconduct — the not doing, not committing, not transgressing the boundary, cutting off the bridge to it — right action, a path factor, included in the path: this is called 'right action'.
Herein, what is right livelihood? The abstaining, avoiding, refraining, abstention from wrong livelihood — the not doing, not committing, not transgressing the boundary, cutting off the bridge to it — right livelihood, a path factor, included in the path: this is called 'right livelihood'.
Herein, what is right effort? The arousing of mental energy... right effort, the enlightenment factor of energy, a path factor, included in the path: this is called 'right effort'.
Herein, what is right mindfulness? The mindfulness, recollection... right mindfulness, the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, a path factor, included in the path: this is called 'right mindfulness'.
Herein, what is right concentration? The steadiness of mind, its stability... right concentration, the enlightenment factor of concentration, a path factor, included in the path: this is called 'right concentration'. This is called 'the path leading to the cessation of suffering'. The remaining states are joined with the path leading to the cessation of suffering. ^2-206

Here, at the time when a monk develops the world-transcending absorption that leads out of the world and leads to the dismantling of accumulation, for the abandoning of wrong views and for reaching the first stage — quite secluded from sense pleasures... he enters and dwells in the first absorption, a difficult practice with slow direct knowledge — at that time contact is present... non-distraction is present. This is called 'the path leading to the cessation of suffering'. ^2-213

214. Herein, what is the origin of suffering? Craving, the remaining defilements, the remaining unwholesome states, the three wholesome roots that are subject to mental taints, and the remaining wholesome states that are subject to mental taints: this is called 'the origin of suffering'.
Herein, what is suffering? The results, subject to mental taints, of wholesome and unwholesome states; those states that are merely functional, being neither wholesome nor unwholesome nor the result of action; and all material form: this is called 'suffering'.
Herein, what is the cessation of suffering? The abandoning of craving, of the remaining defilements, of the remaining unwholesome states, of the three wholesome roots that are subject to mental taints, and of the remaining wholesome states that are subject to mental taints: this is called 'the cessation of suffering'.
Herein, what is the path leading to the cessation of suffering? Here, at the time when a monk develops the world-transcending absorption that leads out of the world and leads to the dismantling of accumulation, for the abandoning of wrong views and for reaching the first stage — quite secluded from sense pleasures... he enters and dwells in the first absorption, a difficult practice with slow direct knowledge — at that time contact is present... non-distraction is present. This is called 'the path leading to the cessation of suffering'.
Abhidhamma Classification. ^2-214

### Analysis of the Faculties ^2-5-0

#### Abhidhamma Classification ^2-5-1-0

219. The twenty-two faculties: the eye faculty, the ear faculty, the nose faculty, the tongue faculty, the body faculty, the mind faculty, the faculty of femininity, the faculty of masculinity, the life faculty, the faculty of pleasure, the faculty of pain, the faculty of joy, the faculty of displeasure, the faculty of equanimity, the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, the faculty of wisdom, the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown", the faculty of full knowledge, the faculty of one who has fully known. ^2-219

220. Herein, what is the eye faculty? The eye that, derived from the four great elements, is a sensitive surface... the empty village: this is called "the eye faculty".
Herein, what is the ear faculty... the nose faculty... the tongue faculty... the body faculty? The body that, derived from the four great elements, is a sensitive surface... the empty village: this is called "the body faculty".
Herein, what is the mind faculty? As one kind, the mind faculty is: joined with contact. As two kinds, the mind faculty is: it may be rooted, or it may be rootless. As three kinds, the mind faculty is: it may be wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral. As four kinds, the mind faculty is: it may belong to the sense sphere, the fine-material sphere, the immaterial sphere, or be unincluded. As five kinds, the mind faculty is: it may be joined with the faculty of pleasure, joined with the faculty of pain, joined with the faculty of joy, joined with the faculty of displeasure, or joined with the faculty of equanimity. As six kinds, the mind faculty is: eye-consciousness... mind-consciousness. This is how, as six kinds, the mind faculty is described.
As seven kinds, the mind faculty is: eye-consciousness... body-consciousness, the mind element, the mind-consciousness element. This is how, as seven kinds, the mind faculty is described.
As eight kinds, the mind faculty is: eye-consciousness... body-consciousness, which may be accompanied by pleasure or accompanied by pain, the mind element, the mind-consciousness element. This is how, as eight kinds, the mind faculty is described.
As nine kinds, the mind faculty is: eye-consciousness... body-consciousness, the mind element, the mind-consciousness element, each of which may be wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral. This is how, as nine kinds, the mind faculty is described.
As ten kinds, the mind faculty is: eye-consciousness... body-consciousness, which may be accompanied by pleasure or accompanied by pain, the mind element, the mind-consciousness element, each of which may be wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral. This is how, as ten kinds, the mind faculty is described... this is how, in many ways, the mind faculty is described. This is called "the mind faculty".
Herein, what is the faculty of femininity? Whatever, in a woman, is the feminine feature, the feminine mark, the feminine behavior, the feminine manner, the feminine condition, the feminine nature: this is called "the faculty of femininity".
Herein, what is the faculty of masculinity? Whatever, in a man, is the masculine feature, the masculine mark, the masculine behavior, the masculine manner, the masculine condition, the masculine nature: this is called "the faculty of masculinity".
Herein, what is the life faculty? As two kinds, the life faculty is: it may be the material life faculty, or it may be the immaterial life faculty.
Herein, what is the material life faculty? Whatever, of those material states, is the lifespan, the persistence, the continuance, the sustaining, the behaving, the carrying-on, the preserving, the life, the life faculty: this is called "the material life faculty".
Herein, what is the immaterial life faculty? Whatever, of those immaterial states, is the lifespan, the persistence, the continuance, the sustaining, the behaving, the carrying-on, the preserving, the life, the life faculty: this is called "the immaterial life faculty". This is called "the life faculty".
Herein, what is the faculty of pleasure? Whatever bodily comfort, bodily pleasure, the pleasant, happy feeling born of bodily contact, the pleasant, happy feeling that is felt and is born of bodily contact: this is called "the faculty of pleasure".
Herein, what is the faculty of pain? Whatever bodily discomfort, bodily pain, the unpleasant, painful feeling born of bodily contact, the unpleasant, painful feeling that is felt and is born of bodily contact: this is called "the faculty of pain".
Herein, what is the faculty of joy? Whatever mental comfort, mental pleasure, the pleasant, happy feeling born of mental contact, the pleasant, happy feeling that is felt and is born of mental contact: this is called "the faculty of joy".
Herein, what is the faculty of displeasure? Whatever mental discomfort, mental pain, the unpleasant, painful feeling born of mental contact, the unpleasant, painful feeling that is felt and is born of mental contact: this is called "the faculty of displeasure".
Herein, what is the faculty of equanimity? Whatever is neither mental comfort nor mental discomfort, the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling born of mental contact, the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling that is felt and is born of mental contact: this is called "the faculty of equanimity".
Herein, what is the faculty of faith? Whatever faith, believing, trusting, confidence, faith, the faculty of faith, the power of faith: this is called "the faculty of faith".
Herein, what is the faculty of energy? Whatever mental arousing of energy, launching out, exertion, endeavoring, striving, zeal, vigor, steadfastness, persistence without slackening, not giving up the desire to act, not putting down the task, taking up the task, energy, the faculty of energy, the power of energy: this is called "the faculty of energy".
Herein, what is the faculty of mindfulness? Whatever mindfulness, recollection, remembering, memory, keeping in mind, not floating away, not forgetting, mindfulness, the faculty of mindfulness, the power of mindfulness, right mindfulness: this is called "the faculty of mindfulness".
Herein, what is the faculty of concentration? Whatever steadiness of mind, its stability, steadfastness, non-distraction, non-wavering, an undistracted state of mind, calm, the faculty of concentration, the power of concentration, right concentration: this is called "the faculty of concentration".
Herein, what is the faculty of wisdom? The wisdom, understanding... non-delusion, investigation of states, right view: this is called "the faculty of wisdom".
Herein, what is the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown"? The wisdom, understanding... non-delusion, investigation of states, right view, the enlightenment factor of investigation of states, a path factor, included in the path, arising for the direct realization of those states not yet known, not yet seen, not yet attained, not yet understood, not yet directly realized: this is called "the faculty of 'I shall come to know the unknown'".
Herein, what is the faculty of full knowledge? The wisdom, understanding... non-delusion, investigation of states, right view, the enlightenment factor of investigation of states, a path factor, included in the path, arising for the direct realization of those states already known, already seen, already attained, already understood, already directly realized: this is called the faculty of full knowledge.
Herein, what is the faculty of one who has fully known? The wisdom, understanding... non-delusion, investigation of states, right view, the enlightenment factor of investigation of states, a path factor, included in the path, arising for one who has fully known, in relation to those states already seen, already attained, already understood, already directly realized: this is called "the faculty of one who has fully known".
Abhidhamma Classification. ^2-220

Questions and Answers.
The Analysis of the Faculties is finished. ^2-224

### Analysis of Dependent Origination ^2-6-0

#### Discourse Classification ^2-6-1-0

225. Dependent on ignorance, formations come to be. Dependent on formations, consciousness comes to be. Dependent on consciousness, mind-and-matter comes to be. Dependent on mind-and-matter, the six sense-fields come to be. Dependent on the six sense-fields, contact comes to be. Dependent on contact, feeling comes to be. Dependent on feeling, craving comes to be. Dependent on craving, clinging comes to be. Dependent on clinging, existence comes to be. Dependent on existence, birth comes to be. Dependent on birth, aging-and-death comes to be, together with sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. Thus does this entire mass of suffering come to be. ^2-225

226. Herein, what is ignorance? Not knowing suffering, not knowing the origin of suffering, not knowing the cessation of suffering, not knowing the way leading to the cessation of suffering: this is called "ignorance".
Herein, what are the formations dependent on ignorance? Merit-producing formations, demerit-producing formations, imperturbable formations, bodily formations, verbal formations, mental formations.
Herein, what is the merit-producing formation? Wholesome volition belonging to the sense sphere and the fine-material sphere, consisting of giving, of virtue, and of meditative development: this is called "the merit-producing formation".
Herein, what is the demerit-producing formation? Unwholesome volition belonging to the sense sphere: this is called "the demerit-producing formation".
Herein, what is the imperturbable formation? Wholesome volition belonging to the immaterial sphere: this is called "the imperturbable formation".
Herein, what is the bodily formation? Bodily volition is the bodily formation, verbal volition is the verbal formation, mental volition is the mental formation. These are called "the formations dependent on ignorance". ^2-226

227. Herein, what is the consciousness dependent on formations? Eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, mind-consciousness: this is called "the consciousness dependent on formations". ^2-227

228. Herein, what is the mind-and-matter dependent on consciousness? There is mind, and there is matter. Herein, what is mind? The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations: this is called "mind". Herein, what is matter? The four great elements, and material form derived from the four great elements: this is called "matter". Thus there is this mind, and this matter. This is called "the mind-and-matter dependent on consciousness". ^2-228

229. Herein, what are the six sense-fields dependent on mind-and-matter? The eye sense-field, the ear sense-field, the nose sense-field, the tongue sense-field, the body sense-field, the mind sense-field: this is called "the six sense-fields dependent on mind-and-matter". ^2-229

230. Herein, what is the contact dependent on the six sense-fields? Eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, mind-contact: this is called "the contact dependent on the six sense-fields". ^2-230

231. Herein, what is the feeling dependent on contact? Feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, feeling born of nose-contact, feeling born of tongue-contact, feeling born of body-contact, feeling born of mind-contact: this is called "the feeling dependent on contact". ^2-231

232. Herein, what is the craving dependent on feeling? Craving for sights, craving for sounds, craving for smells, craving for tastes, craving for tangible objects, craving for mental objects: this is called "the craving dependent on feeling". ^2-232

233. Herein, what is the clinging dependent on craving? Clinging to sense pleasures, clinging to views, clinging to rules and observances, clinging to a doctrine of self: this is called "the clinging dependent on craving". ^2-233

234. Herein, what is the existence dependent on clinging? Existence is of two kinds: there is existence as action, and there is existence as rebirth. Herein, what is existence as action? Merit-producing formations, demerit-producing formations, imperturbable formations: this is called "existence as action". All action that leads to existence is existence as action.
Herein, what is existence as rebirth? Existence in the sense sphere, existence in the fine-material sphere, existence in the immaterial sphere, existence with perception, existence without perception, existence with neither perception nor non-perception, existence with one aggregate, existence with four aggregates, existence with five aggregates: this is called "existence as rebirth". Thus there is this existence as action, and this existence as rebirth. This is called "the existence dependent on clinging". ^2-234

235. Herein, what is the birth dependent on existence? Whatever, for the various beings in the various orders of beings, is birth, coming to birth, descent into the womb, production, the appearance of the aggregates, the obtaining of the sense-fields: this is called "the birth dependent on existence". ^2-235

236. Herein, what is the aging-and-death dependent on birth? There is aging, and there is death. Herein, what is aging? Whatever, for the various beings in the various orders of beings, is aging, decrepitude, broken teeth, grey hair, wrinkled skin, the decline of the lifespan, the wearing out of the faculties: this is called "aging".
Herein, what is death? Whatever, for the various beings from the various orders of beings, is the passing away, the falling away, the breaking up, the disappearance, the dying, the death, the completion of time, the breaking up of the aggregates, the laying down of the body, the cutting off of the life faculty: this is called "death". Thus there is this aging, and this death. This is called "the aging-and-death dependent on birth". ^2-236

237. Herein, what is sorrow? For one touched by the loss of relatives, or touched by the loss of wealth, or touched by the loss of health, or touched by the loss of virtue, or touched by the loss of right view, or possessed of any other kind of loss, or touched by any other kind of painful state: whatever is sorrow, sorrowing, the state of sorrowing, inner sorrow, inner deep sorrow, the burning grief of the mind, grief, the dart of sorrow: this is called "sorrow". ^2-237

238. Herein, what is lamentation? For one touched by the loss of relatives, or touched by the loss of wealth, or touched by the loss of health, or touched by the loss of virtue, or touched by the loss of right view, or possessed of any other kind of loss, or touched by any other kind of painful state: whatever is crying out, lamenting, the state of crying out, the state of lamenting, wailing, weeping, lament, the utterance of laments, wailing speech, the state of wailing speech: this is called "lamentation". ^2-238

239. Herein, what is pain? Whatever bodily discomfort, bodily pain, the unpleasant, painful feeling born of bodily contact, the unpleasant, painful feeling that is felt and is born of bodily contact: this is called "pain". ^2-239

240. Herein, what is grief? Whatever mental discomfort, mental pain, the unpleasant, painful feeling born of mental contact, the unpleasant, painful feeling that is felt and is born of mental contact: this is called "grief". ^2-240

241. Herein, what is despair? For one touched by the loss of relatives, or touched by the loss of wealth, or touched by the loss of health, or touched by the loss of virtue, or touched by the loss of right view, or possessed of any other kind of loss, or touched by any other kind of painful state: whatever is distress, despair, the state of distress, the state of despair: this is called "despair". ^2-241

242. That "thus does this entire mass of suffering come to be" means: thus does this entire mass of suffering come together, meet, unite, and appear. That is why it is said, "thus does this entire mass of suffering come to be."
Discourse Classification. ^2-242

248. Which states are unwholesome? At the time when an unwholesome consciousness has arisen, accompanied by joy, joined with wrong view, having as its object a sight, a sound, a smell, a taste, a tangible object, or a mental object, or whatever else it may be about — at that time, dependent on ignorance, a formation comes to be. Dependent on the formation, consciousness comes to be. Dependent on consciousness, mentality comes to be. Dependent on mentality, the sixth sense-field comes to be. Dependent on the sixth sense-field, contact comes to be. Dependent on contact, feeling comes to be. Dependent on feeling, craving comes to be. Dependent on craving, clinging comes to be. Dependent on clinging, existence comes to be. Dependent on existence, birth comes to be. Dependent on birth, aging-and-death comes to be. Thus does this entire mass of suffering come to be. ^2-248

249. Herein, what is ignorance? Whatever is not knowing, not seeing ... the barrier of ignorance, delusion, the unwholesome root: this is called "ignorance".
Herein, what is the formation dependent on ignorance? Whatever is volition, intention, the state of intending: this is called "the formation dependent on ignorance".
Herein, what is the consciousness dependent on the formation? Whatever is mind, mentality, heart, the pure, mind, the mind sense-field, the mind faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, the corresponding mind-consciousness element: this is called "the consciousness dependent on the formation".
Herein, what is the mentality dependent on consciousness? The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations: this is called "the mentality dependent on consciousness".
Herein, what is the sixth sense-field dependent on mentality? Whatever is mind, mentality, heart, the pure, mind, the mind sense-field, the mind faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, the corresponding mind-consciousness element: this is called "the sixth sense-field dependent on mentality".
Herein, what is the contact dependent on the sixth sense-field? Whatever is contact, touching, the act of touching, the state of touching: this is called "the contact dependent on the sixth sense-field".
Herein, what is the feeling dependent on contact? Whatever mental comfort, mental pleasure, the pleasant, happy feeling born of mental contact, the pleasant, happy feeling that is felt and is born of mental contact: this is called "the feeling dependent on contact".
Herein, what is the craving dependent on feeling? Whatever is lust, infatuation, relishing, approving, delighting, delighting in lust, the mind's infatuation: this is called "the craving dependent on feeling".
Herein, what is the clinging dependent on craving? Whatever is view, a resorting to views, a thicket of views, a wilderness of views, the writhing of views, the vacillation of views, the fetter of views, grasping, insistence, adherence, misapprehension, a wrong path, a false way, wrongness, a sectarian tenet, a distorted grasp: this is called "the clinging dependent on craving".
Herein, what is the existence dependent on clinging? Apart from clinging, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations, the aggregate of consciousness: this is called "the existence dependent on clinging".
Herein, what is the birth dependent on existence? Whatever, of those various states, is birth, coming to birth, production, coming into being, appearance: this is called "the birth dependent on existence".
Herein, what is the aging-and-death dependent on birth? There is aging, and there is death. Herein, what is aging? Whatever, of those various states, is aging, decrepitude, the decline of the lifespan: this is called "aging". Herein, what is death? Whatever, of those various states, is destruction, decay, breaking up, disintegration, impermanence, disappearance: this is called "death". Thus there is this aging, and this death. This is called "the aging-and-death dependent on birth".
That "thus does this entire mass of suffering come to be" means: thus does this entire mass of suffering come together, meet, unite, and appear. That is why it is said, "thus does this entire mass of suffering come to be." ^2-249

Dependent on mind-and-matter, the six sense-fields come to be; and dependent on the sixth sense-field, mind-and-matter too comes to be. Dependent on the sixth sense-field, contact comes to be; and dependent on contact, the sixth sense-field too comes to be. Dependent on contact, feeling comes to be; and dependent on feeling, contact too comes to be. Dependent on feeling, craving comes to be; and dependent on craving, feeling too comes to be. Dependent on craving, clinging comes to be; and dependent on clinging, craving too comes to be. Dependent on clinging, existence comes to be. Dependent on existence, birth comes to be. Dependent on birth, aging-and-death comes to be. Thus does this entire mass of suffering come to be. ^2-278

279. Herein, what is ignorance? Whatever is not knowing, not seeing ... the barrier of ignorance, delusion, the unwholesome root: this is called "ignorance".
Herein, what is the formation dependent on ignorance? Whatever is volition, intention, the state of intending: this is called "the formation dependent on ignorance".
Herein, what is the ignorance that likewise comes to be dependent on the formation? Whatever is not knowing, not seeing ... the barrier of ignorance, delusion, the unwholesome root: this is called "the ignorance that likewise comes to be dependent on the formation".
Herein, what is the consciousness dependent on the formation? Whatever is mind, mentality ... the corresponding mind-consciousness element: this is called "the consciousness dependent on the formation".
Herein, what is the formation that likewise comes to be dependent on consciousness? Whatever is volition, intention, the state of intending: this is called "the formation that likewise comes to be dependent on consciousness".
Herein, what is the mind-and-matter dependent on consciousness? There is mind, and there is matter. Herein, what is mind? The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations: this is called "mind". Herein, what is matter? The growth of the eye sense-field, the growth of the ear sense-field, the growth of the nose sense-field, the growth of the tongue sense-field, the growth of the body sense-field, or whatever other matter there is that is born of mind, caused by mind, arisen from mind: this is called "matter". Thus there is this mind, and this matter. This is called "the mind-and-matter dependent on consciousness".
As for "the consciousness that likewise comes to be dependent on mind-and-matter": there is mind, and there is matter. Herein, what is mind? The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations: this is called "mind". Herein, what is matter? Whatever matter the mind-consciousness element depends on: this is called "matter". Thus there is this mind, and this matter. This is called "mind-and-matter".
Herein, what is the consciousness that likewise comes to be dependent on mind-and-matter? Whatever is mind, mentality ... the corresponding mind-consciousness element: this is called "the consciousness that likewise comes to be dependent on mind-and-matter".
As for "dependent on mind-and-matter, the six sense-fields": there is mind, and there is matter. Herein, what is mind? The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations: this is called "mind". Herein, what is matter? The four great elements, and whatever matter the mind-consciousness element depends on: this is called "matter". Thus there is this mind, and this matter. This is called "mind-and-matter".
Herein, what are the six sense-fields dependent on mind-and-matter? The eye sense-field, the ear sense-field, the nose sense-field, the tongue sense-field, the body sense-field, the mind sense-field: this is called "the six sense-fields dependent on mind-and-matter".
Herein, what is the mind-and-matter that likewise comes to be dependent on the sixth sense-field? There is mind, and there is matter. Herein, what is mind? The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations: this is called "mind". Herein, what is matter? The growth of the eye sense-field, the growth of the ear sense-field, the growth of the nose sense-field, the growth of the tongue sense-field, the growth of the body sense-field, or whatever other matter there is that is born of mind, caused by mind, arisen from mind: this is called "matter". Thus there is this mind, and this matter. This is called "the mind-and-matter that likewise comes to be dependent on the sixth sense-field".
Herein, what is the contact dependent on the sixth sense-field? Whatever is contact, touching, the act of touching, the state of touching: this is called "the contact dependent on the sixth sense-field".
Herein, what is the sixth sense-field that likewise comes to be dependent on contact? Whatever is mind, mentality ... the corresponding mind-consciousness element: this is called "the sixth sense-field that likewise comes to be dependent on contact".
Herein, what is the feeling dependent on contact? Whatever mental comfort, mental pleasure, the pleasant, happy feeling born of mental contact, the pleasant, happy feeling that is felt and is born of mental contact: this is called "the feeling dependent on contact" ... That is why it is said, "thus does this entire mass of suffering come to be."
Tetrad of Mutuality. ^2-279

Dependent on the formation, consciousness comes to be. Dependent on consciousness, mentality comes to be. Dependent on mentality, the sixth sense-field comes to be. Dependent on the sixth sense-field, contact comes to be. Dependent on contact, feeling comes to be. Dependent on feeling, craving comes to be. Dependent on craving, resolve comes to be. Dependent on resolve, existence comes to be. Dependent on existence, birth comes to be. Dependent on birth, aging-and-death comes to be. Thus does this entire mass of suffering come to be. ^2-280

##### Exposition of the Wholesome ^2-6-2-11-0

292. Which states are wholesome? 293. Herein, what are the wholesome roots? Non-greed, non-hatred, non-delusion.
Herein, what is non-greed? Whatever is non-greed, the state of not being greedy, the state of non-greediness, non-infatuation, the state of not being infatuated, the state of non-infatuation, non-covetousness, non-greed, the wholesome root: this is called "non-greed".
Herein, what is non-hatred? Whatever is non-hatred, the state of not hating, the state of non-hatred, non-ill-will, non-malice, non-hatred, the wholesome root: this is called "non-hatred".
Herein, what is non-delusion? Whatever is wisdom, understanding ... non-delusion, investigation of states, right view: this is called "non-delusion". These are called "the wholesome roots".
Herein, what is the formation dependent on a wholesome root? Whatever is volition, intention, the state of intending: this is called "the formation dependent on a wholesome root".
Herein, what is the consciousness dependent on the formation ... the mentality dependent on consciousness ... the sixth sense-field dependent on mentality ... the contact dependent on the sixth sense-field ... the feeling dependent on contact ... this is called "the feeling dependent on contact".
Herein, what is the confidence dependent on feeling? Whatever is faith, believing, trusting, confidence: this is called "the confidence dependent on feeling".
Herein, what is the resolve dependent on confidence? Whatever is the mind's resolve, resolving, the state of being resolved: this is called "the resolve dependent on confidence".
Herein, what is the existence dependent on resolve? Apart from resolve, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations, the aggregate of consciousness: this is called "the existence dependent on resolve" ... That is why it is said, "thus does this entire mass of suffering come to be." ^2-293

Dependent on the sixth sense-field, contact comes to be. Dependent on contact, feeling comes to be. Dependent on feeling, resolve comes to be. Dependent on resolve, existence comes to be. Dependent on existence, birth comes to be. Dependent on birth, aging-and-death comes to be. Thus does this entire mass of suffering come to be. ^2-345

346. Which states are neutral? At the time when, as a result of wholesome sense-sphere action having been done and accumulated, a resultant mind-consciousness element has arisen, accompanied by joy, joined with knowledge ... or accompanied by joy, joined with knowledge, prompted ... or accompanied by joy, dissociated from knowledge ... or accompanied by joy, dissociated from knowledge, prompted ... or accompanied by equanimity, joined with knowledge ... or accompanied by equanimity, joined with knowledge, prompted ... or accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge ... or accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge, prompted, having as its object a sight ... or a mental object, or whatever else it may be about — at that time, dependent on a wholesome root, a formation comes to be. Dependent on the formation, consciousness comes to be. Dependent on consciousness, mentality comes to be. Dependent on mentality, the sixth sense-field comes to be. Dependent on the sixth sense-field, contact comes to be. Dependent on contact, feeling comes to be. Dependent on feeling, confidence comes to be. Dependent on confidence, resolve comes to be. Dependent on resolve, existence comes to be. Dependent on existence, birth comes to be. Dependent on birth, aging-and-death comes to be. Thus does this entire mass of suffering come to be. ^2-346

347. Which states are neutral? At the time when one develops the path to rebirth in the fine-material sphere and, quite secluded from sense pleasures ... enters and dwells in the first jhāna, with the earth-kasiṇa — at that time there is contact ... there is non-distraction: these states are wholesome.
As a result of that same wholesome fine-material-sphere action having been done and accumulated, at the time when — quite secluded from sense pleasures ... one enters and dwells in the first jhāna, with the earth-kasiṇa — at that time, dependent on a wholesome root, a formation comes to be. Dependent on the formation, consciousness comes to be. Dependent on consciousness, mentality comes to be. Dependent on mentality, the sixth sense-field comes to be. Dependent on the sixth sense-field, contact comes to be. Dependent on contact, feeling comes to be. Dependent on feeling, confidence comes to be. Dependent on confidence, resolve comes to be. Dependent on resolve, existence comes to be. Dependent on existence, birth comes to be. Dependent on birth, aging-and-death comes to be. Thus does this entire mass of suffering come to be. ^2-347

348. Which states are neutral? At the time when one develops the path to rebirth in the immaterial sphere and, having completely transcended the base of nothingness, with the perception belonging to the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, and with the abandoning of pleasure ... enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna — at that time there is contact ... there is non-distraction: these states are wholesome.
As a result of that same wholesome immaterial-sphere action having been done and accumulated, at the time when — having completely transcended the base of nothingness, with the perception belonging to the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, and with the abandoning of pleasure ... one enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna — at that time, dependent on a wholesome root, a formation comes to be. Dependent on the formation, consciousness comes to be. Dependent on consciousness, mentality comes to be. Dependent on mentality, the sixth sense-field comes to be. Dependent on the sixth sense-field, contact comes to be. Dependent on contact, feeling comes to be. Dependent on feeling, confidence comes to be. Dependent on confidence, resolve comes to be. Dependent on resolve, existence comes to be. Dependent on existence, birth comes to be. Dependent on birth, aging-and-death comes to be. Thus does this entire mass of suffering come to be. ^2-348

349. Which states are neutral? At the time when one develops the world-transcending jhāna, which leads out, which leads to dismantling, for the abandoning of wrong views, for reaching the first stage, and, quite secluded from sense pleasures ... enters and dwells in the first jhāna — the difficult practice with slow direct knowledge — at that time there is contact ... there is non-distraction: these states are wholesome.
As a result of that same world-transcending wholesome jhāna having been done and developed, at the time when — quite secluded from sense pleasures ... one enters and dwells in the first jhāna — the difficult practice with slow direct knowledge, empty — at that time, dependent on a wholesome root, a formation comes to be. Dependent on the formation, consciousness comes to be. Dependent on consciousness, mentality comes to be. Dependent on mentality, the sixth sense-field comes to be. Dependent on the sixth sense-field, contact comes to be. Dependent on contact, feeling comes to be. Dependent on feeling, confidence comes to be. Dependent on confidence, resolve comes to be. Dependent on resolve, existence comes to be. Dependent on existence, birth comes to be. Dependent on birth, aging-and-death comes to be. Thus does the arising of these states come to be.
