### Analysis of the Absorptions ^2-12-0

#### Discourse Classification ^2-12-1-0

508. Here a monk dwells restrained by the restraint of the code of monastic rules, accomplished in proper conduct and resort, seeing danger in the slightest faults, having undertaken the training he trains in the training rules, guarding the doors of the sense faculties, moderate in food, devoted to wakefulness in the first and last watches of the night, persistent, discerning, and devoted to the development of the states that are aids to awakening. He acts with clear comprehension when going forward and returning; he acts with clear comprehension when looking ahead and looking away; he acts with clear comprehension when bending and stretching his limbs; he acts with clear comprehension when wearing his outer robe, bowl, and robes; he acts with clear comprehension when eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting; he acts with clear comprehension when defecating and urinating; he acts with clear comprehension when walking, standing, sitting, sleeping, waking, speaking, and staying silent. He resorts to a secluded dwelling place: the forest, the foot of a tree, a mountain, a ravine, a hillside cave, a charnel ground, a jungle thicket, the open air, a heap of straw — quiet, with little noise, free from crowds, hidden from people, suitable for retreat. Having gone to the forest, to the foot of a tree, or to an empty dwelling, he sits down, folding his legs crosswise, holding his body straight, and establishing mindfulness in front of him. Having abandoned covetousness for the world, he dwells with a mind free from covetousness; he purifies his mind of covetousness. Having abandoned ill will and hatred, he dwells with a mind free from ill will, sympathetic to the welfare of all living beings; he purifies his mind of ill will and hatred. Having abandoned dullness and drowsiness, he dwells free from dullness and drowsiness, perceiving light, mindful and clearly comprehending; he purifies his mind of dullness and drowsiness. Having abandoned restlessness and remorse, he dwells unagitated, with a mind inwardly calmed; he purifies his mind of restlessness and remorse. Having abandoned doubt, he dwells having crossed over doubt, unperplexed about wholesome states; he purifies his mind of doubt. Having abandoned these five hindrances, the corruptions of the mind that weaken wisdom, quite secluded from sense pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, he enters and dwells in the first absorption, accompanied by applied and sustained thought, with joy and happiness born of seclusion. With the stilling of applied and sustained thought, he enters and dwells in the second absorption, which has internal confidence and concentration of mind, is without applied thought and without sustained thought, and has joy and happiness born of concentration. With the fading away of joy, he dwells with equanimity, mindful and clearly comprehending, and experiences happiness with the body; he enters and dwells in the third absorption, of which the noble ones say: "one of equanimity and mindfulness dwells happily". With the abandoning of happiness and the abandoning of pain, and with the earlier disappearance of gladness and sadness, he enters and dwells in the fourth absorption, which is neither painful nor pleasant, and which has purity of mindfulness through equanimity. With the complete transcending of perceptions of material form, with the disappearance of perceptions of resistance, and with non-attention to perceptions of diversity, aware that "space is infinite", he enters and dwells in the base of infinite space. With the complete transcending of the base of infinite space, aware that "consciousness is infinite", he enters and dwells in the base of infinite consciousness. With the complete transcending of the base of infinite consciousness, aware that "there is nothing", he enters and dwells in the base of nothingness. With the complete transcending of the base of nothingness, he enters and dwells in the base of neither perception nor non-perception. ^2-508

##### Matrix ^2-12-1-1-0

509. As to "here": in this view, in this acceptance, in this preference, in this doctrine, in this teaching, in this discipline, in this teaching-and-discipline, in this proclamation, in this holy life, in this Teacher's dispensation. Therefore it is called "here". ^2-509

510. As to "monk": a monk by convention, a monk by acknowledgement, one who is a monk because he begs, one who is a monk because of the state of having gone forth to beg, one who is a monk because he has taken up the practice of begging, one who is a monk because he wears a patched-together robe, one who is a monk because he breaks up bad, unwholesome states, one who is a monk because of having broken bad, unwholesome states, one who is a monk through the partial abandoning of defilements, one who is a monk through the total abandoning of defilements, a monk in higher training, a monk beyond training, a monk who is neither in higher training nor beyond it, a foremost monk, a good monk, a pure monk, a monk of true worth, a monk who has received the full ordination through a legitimate act of the Community consisting of a motion and three announcements, an act that is unshakable and fit to stand. ^2-510

511. As to "the code": virtue, foundation, beginning, good conduct, restraint, control, release, the foremost among the attainment of wholesome states. As to "restraint": non-transgression by body, non-transgression by speech, non-transgression by body and speech. As to "restrained": one who is endowed with, fully endowed with, arrived at, fully arrived at, attained, fully attained, and possesses this restraint by the code. Therefore it is called "restrained by the restraint of the code". ^2-511

512. As to "dwells": he behaves, conducts himself, maintains himself, keeps himself going, carries on, lives, dwells. Therefore it is called "dwells". ^2-512

513. As to "accomplished in proper conduct and resort": there is conduct, and there is misconduct.
Herein, what is misconduct? Transgression by body, transgression by speech, transgression by body and speech: this is called "misconduct". All immorality is misconduct. Here someone makes a living by one means or another of wrong livelihood condemned by the Buddha: by giving bamboo, giving leaves, giving flowers, giving fruit, giving bath powder, giving tooth-wood, by flattery, by fawning for the sake of soup, by ingratiating gift-giving, or by running errands: this is called "misconduct".
Herein, what is conduct? Non-transgression by body, non-transgression by speech, non-transgression by body and speech: this is called "conduct". All restraint by virtue is conduct. Here someone does not make a living by such a wrong livelihood condemned by the Buddha — not by giving bamboo, not by giving leaves, not by giving flowers, not by giving fruit, not by giving bath powder, not by giving tooth-wood, not by flattery, not by fawning for the sake of soup, not by ingratiating gift-giving, and not by running errands: this is called "conduct". ^2-513

514. As to "resort": there is proper resort, and there is improper resort.
Herein, what is improper resort? Here someone frequents the resort of prostitutes, the resort of widows, the resort of unmarried women, the resort of eunuchs, the resort of nuns, or the resort of taverns; he lives mixed up with kings, kings' ministers, sectarians, and sectarian disciples in an unsuitable association; or he associates with, frequents, and attends on families that are without faith, without confidence, that are not a source of support, that abuse and revile, that do not wish well, do not wish for benefit, do not wish for comfort, and do not wish for security for monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen: this is called "improper resort".
Herein, what is proper resort? Here someone does not frequent the resort of prostitutes, the resort of widows, the resort of unmarried women, the resort of eunuchs, the resort of nuns, or the resort of taverns; he does not live mixed up with kings, kings' ministers, sectarians, and sectarian disciples in an unsuitable association; but he associates with, frequents, and attends on families that have faith, that have confidence, that are a source of support, adorned with the ochre robe, welcoming to renunciants, that wish well, wish for benefit, wish for comfort, and wish for security for monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen: this is called "proper resort". Thus he is endowed with, fully endowed with... possesses both this conduct and this resort. Therefore it is called "accomplished in proper conduct and resort". ^2-514

515. As to "seeing danger in the slightest faults": herein, what are the slightest faults? Those faults that are minor, small, light, considered light, requiring restraint, requiring control, requiring watchfulness of the mind, and bound up with attention — these are called "the slightest faults". Thus, with regard to these slightest faults, he sees the fault, sees the danger, sees the drawback, and sees the escape. Therefore it is called "seeing danger in the slightest faults". ^2-515

516. As to "having undertaken the training, he trains in the training rules": herein, what is the training? There are four trainings: the training of monks for monks, the training of nuns for nuns, the training of laymen for laymen, the training of laywomen for laywomen. These are called "the trainings". Thus, with regard to these trainings, he undertakes and conducts himself in accordance with them completely, in every way, without exception, leaving nothing out. Therefore it is called "having undertaken the training, he trains in the training rules". ^2-516

517. As to "guarding the doors of the sense faculties": there is guarding the doors of the sense faculties, and there is not guarding the doors.
Herein, what is not guarding the doors of the sense faculties? Here someone, on seeing a form with the eye, grasps at its sign and its features. Since, if he dwells with the eye faculty unrestrained, bad, unwholesome states of covetousness and displeasure might flow in upon him, he does not practise for its restraint, does not guard the eye faculty, does not undertake restraint of the eye faculty. On hearing a sound with the ear... on smelling an odour with the nose... on tasting a flavour with the tongue... on touching a tangible with the body... on cognizing a mental object with the mind, he grasps at its sign and its features. Since, if he dwells with the mind faculty unrestrained, bad, unwholesome states of covetousness and displeasure might flow in upon him, he does not practise for its restraint, does not guard the mind faculty, does not undertake restraint of the mind faculty. Whatever lack of guarding, lack of protection, lack of watching over, and lack of restraint there is with regard to these six faculties: this is called "not guarding the doors of the sense faculties".
Herein, what is guarding the doors of the sense faculties? Here someone, on seeing a form with the eye, does not grasp at its sign and does not grasp at its features. Since, if he dwells with the eye faculty unrestrained, bad, unwholesome states of covetousness and displeasure might flow in upon him, he practises for its restraint, guards the eye faculty, undertakes restraint of the eye faculty. On hearing a sound with the ear... on smelling an odour with the nose... on tasting a flavour with the tongue... on touching a tangible with the body... on cognizing a mental object with the mind, he does not grasp at its sign and does not grasp at its features. Since, if he dwells with the mind faculty unrestrained, bad, unwholesome states of covetousness and displeasure might flow in upon him, he practises for its restraint, guards the mind faculty, undertakes restraint of the mind faculty. Whatever guarding, protection, watching over, and restraint there is with regard to these six faculties: this is called "guarding the doors of the sense faculties". He is endowed with, fully endowed with... possesses this guarding of the doors of the sense faculties. Therefore it is called "guarding the doors of the sense faculties". ^2-517

518. As to "moderate in food": there is moderation in food, and there is immoderation in food.
Herein, what is immoderation in food? Here someone eats food without reflection, unwisely, for amusement, for intoxication, for beautification, for adornment. Whatever lack of contentment, immoderation, and lack of reflection with regard to food there is: this is called "immoderation in food".
Herein, what is moderation in food? Here someone eats food with reflection, wisely: "not for amusement, not for intoxication, not for beautification, not for adornment, but only for the maintenance and continuation of this body, for keeping it free from harm, for supporting the holy life, thinking: 'thus I shall put an end to the old feeling and not arouse a new feeling, and I shall be healthy, blameless, and live in comfort.'" Whatever contentment, moderation, and reflection with regard to food there is: this is called "moderation in food". He is endowed with, fully endowed with... possesses this moderation in food. Therefore it is called "moderate in food". ^2-518

519. And how is a monk devoted to wakefulness in the first and last watches of the night? Here a monk purifies his mind of obstructive states by walking back and forth and sitting during the day; in the first watch of the night, he purifies his mind of obstructive states by walking back and forth and sitting; in the middle watch of the night, he lies down on his right side in the lion's posture, one foot placed upon the other, mindful and clearly comprehending, having noted in his mind the time for rising; in the last watch of the night, having risen, he purifies his mind of obstructive states by walking back and forth and sitting. In this way a monk is devoted to wakefulness in the first and last watches of the night. ^2-519

520. As to "persistent": whatever mental arousing of energy... right effort. ^2-520

521. As to "discerning": whatever wisdom, understanding... non-delusion, investigation of states, right view. ^2-521

522. As to "devoted to the development of the states that are aids to awakening": herein, what are the states that are aids to awakening? The seven awakening factors: the factor of mindfulness, the factor of investigation, the factor of energy, the factor of joy, the factor of tranquillity, the factor of concentration, the factor of equanimity. These are called "the states that are aids to awakening". Thus he cultivates, develops, and pursues these states that are aids to awakening. Therefore it is called "devoted to the development of the states that are aids to awakening". ^2-522

523. And how does a monk act with clear comprehension when going forward and returning, act with clear comprehension when looking ahead and looking away, act with clear comprehension when bending and stretching his limbs, act with clear comprehension when wearing his outer robe, bowl, and robes, act with clear comprehension when eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting, act with clear comprehension when defecating and urinating, act with clear comprehension when walking, standing, sitting, sleeping, waking, speaking, and staying silent? Here a monk, mindful and clearly comprehending, goes forward; mindful and clearly comprehending, he returns; mindful and clearly comprehending, he looks ahead; mindful and clearly comprehending, he looks away; mindful and clearly comprehending, he bends his limbs; mindful and clearly comprehending, he stretches his limbs; he acts with clear comprehension, mindful; he acts with clear comprehension, mindful, when wearing his outer robe, bowl, and robes; he acts with clear comprehension, mindful, when eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting; he acts with clear comprehension, mindful, when defecating and urinating; he acts with clear comprehension, mindful, when walking, standing, sitting, sleeping, waking, speaking, and staying silent. ^2-523

524. Herein, what is mindfulness? Whatever mindfulness, recollection, remembering, memory, keeping in mind, not floating away, not forgetting, mindfulness, the faculty of mindfulness, the power of mindfulness, right mindfulness: this is called "mindfulness". ^2-524

525. As to "clearly comprehending": herein, what is clear comprehension? Whatever wisdom, understanding, discernment, examination, investigation of states, differentiation, discerning, discrimination, clarification, skill, erudition, breadth of wisdom, thought, consideration, breadth and keenness of wisdom, guidance, insight, clear comprehension, the goad, wisdom, the faculty of wisdom, the power of wisdom, the sword of wisdom, the tower of wisdom, the lamp of wisdom, the radiance of wisdom, the beacon of wisdom, the jewel of wisdom, non-delusion, investigation of states, right view: this is called "clear comprehension". Thus he is endowed with, fully endowed with... possesses this mindfulness and this clear comprehension. In this way a monk, mindful and clearly comprehending, goes forward; mindful and clearly comprehending, he returns; mindful and clearly comprehending, he looks ahead; mindful and clearly comprehending, he looks away; mindful and clearly comprehending, he bends his limbs; mindful and clearly comprehending, he stretches his limbs; he acts with clear comprehension, mindful; he acts with clear comprehension, mindful, when wearing his outer robe, bowl, and robes; he acts with clear comprehension, mindful, when eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting; he acts with clear comprehension, mindful, when defecating and urinating; he acts with clear comprehension, mindful, when walking, standing, sitting, sleeping, waking, speaking, and staying silent. ^2-525

526. As to "secluded": even if a dwelling place is nearby, if it is not crowded with householders and renunciants, then it is secluded. Even if a dwelling place is far away, if it is not crowded with householders and renunciants, then it is secluded. ^2-526

527. As to "dwelling place": a bed is also a dwelling place, a chair is also a dwelling place, a mattress is also a dwelling place, a pillow is also a dwelling place, a monastery is also a dwelling place, a lean-to is also a dwelling place, a mansion is also a dwelling place, a watchtower is also a dwelling place, a hall is also a dwelling place, a cave is also a dwelling place, a grotto is also a dwelling place, the foot of a tree is also a dwelling place, a bamboo grove is also a dwelling place. Indeed, wherever monks stay, all of this is a dwelling place. ^2-527

528. As to "resorts to a secluded dwelling place": he resorts to, frequents, cultivates, follows, and pursues this secluded dwelling place. Therefore it is called "resorts to a secluded dwelling place". ^2-528

529. As to "the forest": having gone out beyond the boundary post, all of that is the forest. ^2-529

530. As to "the foot of a tree": the foot of a tree is just the foot of a tree. A mountain is just a mountain. A ravine is just a ravine. A hillside cave is just a hillside cave. A charnel ground is just a charnel ground. The open air is just the open air. A heap of straw is just a heap of straw. ^2-530

531. As to "jungle thicket": this is a designation for dwelling places that are remote. As to "jungle thicket": this is a designation for dwelling places that are wooded groves. As to "jungle thicket": this is a designation for dwelling places that are frightening. As to "jungle thicket": this is a designation for dwelling places that cause the hair to stand on end. As to "jungle thicket": this is a designation for dwelling places that are on the outskirts. As to "jungle thicket": this is a designation for dwelling places not frequented by people. As to "jungle thicket": this is a designation for dwelling places difficult to reach. ^2-531

532. As to "with little noise": even if a dwelling place is nearby, if it is not crowded with householders and renunciants, then it has little noise. Even if a dwelling place is far away, if it is not crowded with householders and renunciants, then it has little noise. ^2-532

533. As to "free from crowds": whatever has little noise, that is free from crowds. Whatever is free from crowds, that is untouched by the bustle of people. Whatever is untouched by the bustle of people, that is hidden from people. Whatever is hidden from people, that is suitable for retreat. ^2-533

534. As to "having gone to the forest, to the foot of a tree, or to an empty dwelling": he has gone to the forest, or to the foot of a tree, or to an empty dwelling. ^2-534

535. As to "sits down, folding his legs crosswise": he is seated, having folded his legs crosswise. ^2-535

536. As to "holding his body straight": the body is upright, steady, and well set. ^2-536

537. As to "establishing mindfulness in front of him": herein, what is mindfulness? Whatever mindfulness, recollection, remembering... right mindfulness: this is called "mindfulness". This mindfulness is established, well established, at the tip of the nose or at the sign of the mouth. Therefore it is called "establishing mindfulness in front of him". ^2-537

538. As to "having abandoned covetousness for the world": herein, what is covetousness? Whatever lust, passion... the mind's passion: this is called "covetousness".
Herein, what is the world? The five aggregates subject to clinging are the world: this is called "the world". This covetousness, with regard to this world, is removed, thoroughly removed, calmed, stilled, settled, ended, fully ended, quenched, extinguished, dried up, thoroughly dried up, and brought to an end. Therefore it is called "having abandoned covetousness for the world". ^2-538

539. As to "with a mind free from covetousness": herein, what is mind? Whatever mind, mental activity... the corresponding mind-consciousness element: this is called "mind". This mind is free from covetousness. Therefore it is called "with a mind free from covetousness". ^2-539

540. As to "dwells": he behaves, conducts himself, maintains himself, keeps himself going, carries on, lives, dwells. Therefore it is called "dwells". ^2-540

541. As to "he purifies his mind of covetousness": herein, what is covetousness? Whatever lust, passion... the mind's passion: this is called "covetousness".
Herein, what is mind? Whatever mind, mental activity... the corresponding mind-consciousness element: this is called "mind". This mind is cleansed, thoroughly cleansed, purified, released, thoroughly released, and fully released from this covetousness. Therefore it is called "he purifies his mind of covetousness". ^2-541

542. As to "having abandoned ill will and hatred": there is ill will, and there is hatred.
Herein, what is ill will? Whatever resentment, hostility, opposition, hostile opposition, anger, irritation, being enraged, hate, malice, being malicious, the mind's malice, mental hatred, wrath, becoming wrathful, the state of having become wrathful, hate, hating, the state of hating, hostility, becoming hostile, the state of having become hostile, opposition, hostile opposition, fierceness, harshness, and displeasure of mind: this is called "ill will".
Herein, what is hatred? Whatever is ill will, that is hatred; whatever is hatred, that is ill will. Thus this ill will and this hatred are removed, thoroughly removed, calmed, stilled, settled, ended, fully ended, quenched, extinguished, dried up, thoroughly dried up, and brought to an end. Therefore it is called "having abandoned ill will and hatred". ^2-542

543. As to "a mind free from ill will": herein, what is mind? Whatever mind, mental activity... the corresponding mind-consciousness element: this is called "mind". This mind is free from ill will. Therefore it is called "a mind free from ill will". ^2-543

544. As to "dwells"... therefore it is called "dwells". ^2-544

545. As to "he purifies his mind of ill will and hatred": there is ill will, and there is hatred.
Herein, what is ill will? Whatever resentment of mind... fierceness, harshness, and displeasure of mind: this is called "ill will".
Herein, what is hatred? Whatever is ill will, that is hatred; whatever is hatred, that is ill will.
Herein, what is mind? Whatever mind, mental activity... the corresponding mind-consciousness element: this is called "mind". This mind is cleansed, thoroughly cleansed, purified, released, thoroughly released, and fully released from this ill will and hatred. Therefore it is called "he purifies his mind of ill will and hatred". ^2-545

546. As to "having abandoned dullness and drowsiness": there is dullness, and there is drowsiness.
Herein, what is dullness? Whatever unwieldiness, unworkableness, sinking, shrinking, the shrunken state, sinking down, the state of having sunk down, dullness, becoming dull, the state of having become dull in the mind: this is called "dullness".
Herein, what is drowsiness? Whatever unwieldiness, unworkableness of the body, torpor, enveloping torpor, being closed in, drowsiness, sleepiness, nodding off, sleepiness, becoming sleepy, the state of having become sleepy: this is called "drowsiness". Thus this dullness and this drowsiness are removed, thoroughly removed, calmed, stilled, settled, ended, fully ended, quenched, extinguished, dried up, thoroughly dried up, and brought to an end. Therefore it is called "having abandoned dullness and drowsiness". ^2-546

547. As to "free from dullness and drowsiness": because that dullness and drowsiness has been given up, vomited out, released, abandoned, relinquished, and abandoned and relinquished. Therefore it is called "free from dullness and drowsiness". ^2-547

548. As to "dwells"... therefore it is called "dwells". ^2-548

549. As to "perceiving light": herein, what is perception? Whatever perception, perceiving, the state of having perceived: this is called "perception". This perception is luminous, open, pure, and bright. Therefore it is called "perceiving light". ^2-549

550. As to "mindful and clearly comprehending": herein, what is mindfulness? Whatever mindfulness, recollection... right mindfulness: this is called "mindfulness".
Herein, what is clear comprehension? Whatever wisdom, understanding... non-delusion, investigation of states, right view: this is called "clear comprehension". Thus he is endowed with, fully endowed with... possesses this mindfulness and this clear comprehension. Therefore it is called "mindful and clearly comprehending". ^2-550

551. As to "he purifies his mind of dullness and drowsiness": there is dullness, and there is drowsiness.
Herein, what is dullness... this is called "dullness".
Herein, what is drowsiness... this is called "drowsiness".
Herein, what is mind... this is called "mind". This mind is cleansed, thoroughly cleansed, purified, released, thoroughly released, and fully released from this dullness and drowsiness. Therefore it is called "he purifies his mind of dullness and drowsiness". ^2-551

552. As to "having abandoned restlessness and remorse": there is restlessness, and there is remorse.
Herein, what is restlessness? Whatever restlessness of mind, unsettledness, agitation of mind, distraction of mind: this is called "restlessness".
Herein, what is remorse? Perceiving as allowable what is not allowable, perceiving as not allowable what is allowable, perceiving as blameworthy what is not blameworthy, perceiving as not blameworthy what is blameworthy — whatever remorse of this kind, worrying, the state of worrying, regret of mind, and mental scruple there is: this is called "remorse". Thus this restlessness and this remorse are removed, thoroughly removed, calmed, stilled, settled, ended, fully ended, quenched, extinguished, dried up, thoroughly dried up, and brought to an end. Therefore it is called "having abandoned restlessness and remorse". ^2-552

553. As to "unagitated": because that restlessness and remorse has been given up, vomited out, released, abandoned, relinquished, and abandoned and relinquished. Therefore it is called "unagitated". ^2-553

554. As to "dwells"... therefore it is called "dwells". ^2-554

555. As to "a mind inwardly calmed": herein, what is mind? Whatever mind, mental activity... the corresponding mind-consciousness element: this is called "mind". This mind is inwardly peaceful, calmed, and stilled. Therefore it is called "a mind inwardly calmed". ^2-555

556. As to "he purifies his mind of restlessness and remorse": there is restlessness, and there is remorse.
Herein, what is restlessness? Whatever restlessness of mind, unsettledness, agitation of mind, distraction of mind: this is called "restlessness".
Herein, what is remorse... this is called "remorse".
Herein, what is mind... this is called "mind". This mind is cleansed, thoroughly cleansed, purified, released, thoroughly released, and fully released from this restlessness and remorse. Therefore it is called "he purifies his mind of restlessness and remorse". ^2-556

557. As to "having abandoned doubt": herein, what is doubt? Whatever doubt, doubting, the state of doubting, uncertainty, doubt, being of two minds, being at a fork in the road, questioning, holding to more than one view, groping, casting about, failure to grasp, and bewilderment of mind: this is called "doubt". This doubt is removed, thoroughly removed, calmed, stilled, settled, ended, fully ended, quenched, extinguished, dried up, thoroughly dried up, and brought to an end. Therefore it is called "having abandoned doubt". ^2-557

558. As to "having crossed over doubt": he has crossed over, thoroughly crossed over, gone beyond, reached the far shore of, and arrived at the far shore of this doubt. Therefore it is called "having crossed over doubt". ^2-558

559. As to "unperplexed about wholesome states": because of this doubt, he does not doubt, does not have uncertainty, is unperplexed, free from perplexity, and rid of perplexity concerning wholesome states. Therefore it is called "unperplexed about wholesome states". ^2-559

560. As to "he purifies his mind of doubt": herein, what is doubt? Whatever doubt, doubting, the state of doubting, and bewilderment of mind: this is called "doubt".
Herein, what is mind? Whatever mind, mental activity... the corresponding mind-consciousness element: this is called "mind". This mind is cleansed, thoroughly cleansed, purified, released, thoroughly released, and fully released from this doubt. Therefore it is called "he purifies his mind of doubt". ^2-560

561. As to "having abandoned these five hindrances": these five hindrances are removed, thoroughly removed, calmed, stilled, settled, ended, fully ended, quenched, extinguished, dried up, thoroughly dried up, and brought to an end. Therefore it is called "having abandoned these five hindrances". ^2-561

562. As to "the corruptions of the mind": these five hindrances are corruptions of the mind. ^2-562

563. As to "that weaken wisdom": because of these five hindrances, wisdom that has not arisen does not arise, and wisdom that has arisen ceases. Therefore it is called "that weaken wisdom". ^2-563

564. As to "quite secluded from sense pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states": herein, what are sense pleasures? Desire is a sense pleasure, lust is a sense pleasure, desire-and-lust is a sense pleasure, thinking is a sense pleasure, lust is a sense pleasure, thinking-and-lust is a sense pleasure: these are called "sense pleasures".
Herein, what are the unwholesome states? Sense desire, ill will, dullness, drowsiness, restlessness, remorse, doubt: these are called "the unwholesome states". Thus he is secluded from these sense pleasures and from these unwholesome states. Therefore it is called "quite secluded from sense pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states". ^2-564

565. As to "accompanied by applied and sustained thought": there is applied thought, and there is sustained thought.
Herein, what is applied thought? Whatever thinking, thought, intention, fixing, focusing, directing of the mind, right intention: this is called "applied thought".
Herein, what is sustained thought? Whatever examining, sustained thought, continuous examination, close examination, connection of mind, and scrutiny: this is called "sustained thought". Thus he is endowed with, fully endowed with... possesses this applied thought and this sustained thought. Therefore it is called "accompanied by applied and sustained thought". ^2-565

566. As to "born of seclusion": applied thought, sustained thought, joy, happiness, and one-pointedness of mind — these are born, well born, produced, well produced, and manifested in this seclusion. Therefore it is called "born of seclusion". ^2-566

567. As to "joy and happiness": there is joy, and there is happiness.
Herein, what is joy? Whatever joy, delight, rejoicing, gladdening, mirth, merriment, elation, exultation, and satisfaction of mind: this is called "joy".
Herein, what is happiness? Whatever mental comfort, mental happiness, the comfortable, happy experience born of mental contact, the comfortable, happy feeling born of mental contact: this is called "happiness". This happiness is accompanied by, co-arisen with, conjoined with, and joined with this joy. Therefore it is called "joy and happiness". ^2-567

568. As to "first": it is first in numerical order. One attains this as the first: therefore it is "first". ^2-568

569. As to "absorption": applied thought, sustained thought, joy, happiness, and one-pointedness of mind. ^2-569

570. As to "enters and dwells in": whatever gain, attainment, achievement, accomplishment, touching, realizing, and reaching of the first absorption there is. ^2-570

571. As to "dwells"... therefore it is called "dwells". ^2-571

572. As to "with the stilling of applied and sustained thought": there is applied thought, and there is sustained thought.
Herein, what is applied thought? Whatever thinking, thought... right intention: this is called "applied thought".
Herein, what is sustained thought? Whatever examining, sustained thought, continuous examination, close examination, connection of mind, and scrutiny: this is called "sustained thought". Thus this applied thought and this sustained thought are removed, thoroughly removed, calmed, stilled, settled, ended, fully ended, quenched, extinguished, dried up, thoroughly dried up, and brought to an end. Therefore it is called "with the stilling of applied and sustained thought". ^2-572

573. As to "internal": whatever is internal, individual. ^2-573

574. As to "confidence": whatever faith, trusting, confiding, and full confidence there is. ^2-574

575. As to "concentration of mind": whatever steadiness of mind... right concentration. ^2-575

576. As to "without applied thought and without sustained thought": there is applied thought, and there is sustained thought.
Herein, what is applied thought? Whatever thinking, thought... right intention: this is called "applied thought".
Herein, what is sustained thought? Whatever examining, continuous examining, sustained thought, continuous examination, close examination, connection of mind, and scrutiny: this is called "sustained thought". Thus this applied thought and this sustained thought are removed, thoroughly removed, calmed, stilled, settled, ended, fully ended, quenched, extinguished, dried up, thoroughly dried up, and brought to an end. Therefore it is called "without applied thought and without sustained thought". ^2-576

577. As to "born of concentration": confidence, joy, and happiness — these are born, well born, produced, well produced, and manifested in this concentration. Therefore it is called "born of concentration". ^2-577

578. As to "joy and happiness": there is joy, and there is happiness.
Herein, what is joy... this is called "joy".
Herein, what is happiness... this is called "happiness". This happiness is accompanied by, co-arisen with, conjoined with, and joined with this joy. Therefore it is called "joy and happiness". ^2-578

579. As to "second": it is second in numerical order. One attains this as the second: therefore it is "second". ^2-579

580. As to "absorption": confidence, joy, happiness, and one-pointedness of mind. ^2-580

581. As to "enters and dwells in": whatever gain, attainment, achievement, accomplishment, touching, realizing, and reaching of the second absorption there is. ^2-581

582. As to "dwells"... therefore it is called "dwells". ^2-582

583. As to "with the fading away of joy": herein, what is joy? Whatever joy, delight, rejoicing, gladdening, mirth, merriment, elation, exultation, and satisfaction of mind: this is called "joy". This joy is removed, thoroughly removed, calmed, stilled, settled, ended, fully ended, quenched, extinguished, dried up, thoroughly dried up, and brought to an end. Therefore it is called "with the fading away of joy". ^2-583

584. As to "with equanimity": herein, what is equanimity? Whatever equanimity, looking on, looking on with equanimity, and neutrality of mind: this is called "equanimity". He is endowed with, fully endowed with... possesses this equanimity. Therefore it is called "with equanimity". ^2-584

585. As to "dwells"... therefore it is called "dwells". ^2-585

586. As to "mindful and clearly comprehending": herein, what is mindfulness? Whatever mindfulness, recollection... right mindfulness: this is called "mindfulness".
Herein, what is clear comprehension? Whatever wisdom, understanding... non-delusion, investigation of states, right view: this is called "clear comprehension". Thus he is endowed with, fully endowed with... possesses this mindfulness and this clear comprehension. Therefore it is called "mindful and clearly comprehending". ^2-586

587. As to "experiences happiness with the body": herein, what is happiness? Whatever mental comfort, mental happiness, the comfortable, happy experience born of mental contact, the comfortable, happy feeling born of mental contact: this is called "happiness".
Herein, what is the body? The aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations, the aggregate of consciousness: this is called "the body". He experiences this happiness with this body. Therefore it is called "experiences happiness with the body". ^2-587

588. As to "of which the noble ones say": herein, who are the noble ones? The noble ones are called the Buddhas and the Buddhas' disciples. They say this, teach it, make it known, establish it, explain it, analyze it, make it plain, and reveal it. Therefore it is called "of which the noble ones say". ^2-588

589. As to "one of equanimity and mindfulness dwells happily": herein, what is equanimity? Whatever equanimity, looking on, looking on with equanimity, and neutrality of mind: this is called "equanimity".
Herein, what is mindfulness? Whatever mindfulness, recollection... right mindfulness: this is called "mindfulness".
Herein, what is happiness? Whatever mental comfort, mental happiness, the comfortable, happy experience born of mental contact, the comfortable, happy feeling born of mental contact: this is called "happiness". Thus, possessing this equanimity, this mindfulness, and this happiness, he behaves, conducts himself, maintains himself, keeps himself going, carries on, lives, and dwells. Therefore it is called "one of equanimity and mindfulness dwells happily". ^2-589

590. As to "third": it is third in numerical order. One attains this as the third: therefore it is "third". ^2-590

591. As to "absorption": equanimity, mindfulness, clear comprehension, happiness, and one-pointedness of mind. ^2-591

592. As to "enters and dwells in": whatever gain, attainment, achievement, accomplishment, touching, realizing, and reaching of the third absorption there is. ^2-592

593. As to "dwells"... therefore it is called "dwells". ^2-593

594. As to "with the abandoning of happiness and the abandoning of pain": there is happiness, and there is pain.
Herein, what is happiness? Whatever bodily comfort, bodily happiness, the comfortable, happy experience born of bodily contact, the comfortable, happy feeling born of bodily contact: this is called "happiness".
Herein, what is pain? Whatever bodily discomfort, bodily pain, the uncomfortable, painful experience born of bodily contact, the uncomfortable, painful feeling born of bodily contact: this is called "pain". Thus this happiness and this pain are removed, thoroughly removed, calmed, stilled, settled, ended, fully ended, quenched, extinguished, dried up, thoroughly dried up, and brought to an end. Therefore it is called "with the abandoning of happiness and the abandoning of pain". ^2-594

595. As to "with the earlier disappearance of gladness and sadness": there is gladness, and there is sadness.
Herein, what is gladness? Whatever mental comfort, mental happiness, the comfortable, happy experience born of mental contact, the comfortable, happy feeling born of mental contact: this is called "gladness".
Herein, what is sadness? Whatever mental discomfort, mental pain, the uncomfortable, painful experience born of mental contact, the uncomfortable, painful feeling born of mental contact: this is called "sadness". Thus this gladness and this sadness, already before this, are removed, thoroughly removed, calmed, stilled, settled, ended, fully ended, quenched, extinguished, dried up, thoroughly dried up, and brought to an end. Therefore it is called "with the earlier disappearance of gladness and sadness". ^2-595

596. As to "neither painful nor pleasant": whatever mental feeling that is neither comfortable nor uncomfortable, the neither-painful-nor-pleasant experience born of mental contact, the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling born of mental contact. Therefore it is called "neither painful nor pleasant". ^2-596

597. As to "purity of mindfulness through equanimity": herein, what is equanimity? Whatever equanimity, looking on, looking on with equanimity, and neutrality of mind: this is called "equanimity".
Herein, what is mindfulness? Whatever mindfulness, recollection... right mindfulness: this is called "mindfulness". This mindfulness, through this equanimity, is opened up, purified, and made bright. Therefore it is called "purity of mindfulness through equanimity". ^2-597

598. As to "fourth": it is fourth in numerical order. One attains this as the fourth: therefore it is "fourth". ^2-598

599. As to "absorption": equanimity, mindfulness, and one-pointedness of mind. ^2-599

600. As to "enters and dwells in": whatever gain, attainment, achievement, accomplishment, touching, realizing, and reaching of the fourth absorption there is. ^2-600

601. As to "dwells"... therefore it is called "dwells". ^2-601

602. As to "with the complete transcending of perceptions of material form": herein, what are perceptions of material form? Whatever perception, perceiving, the state of having perceived belonging to one who has attained, or been reborn through, or dwells happily here and now in a fine-material-sphere attainment: these are called "perceptions of material form". These perceptions of material form are transcended, thoroughly transcended, completely transcended. Therefore it is called "with the complete transcending of perceptions of material form". ^2-602

603. As to "with the disappearance of perceptions of resistance": herein, what are perceptions of resistance? Perception of forms, perception of sounds... perception of tangibles: these are called "perceptions of resistance". These perceptions of resistance are removed, thoroughly removed, calmed, stilled, settled, ended, fully ended, quenched, extinguished, dried up, thoroughly dried up, and brought to an end. Therefore it is called "with the disappearance of perceptions of resistance". ^2-603

604. As to "with non-attention to perceptions of diversity": herein, what are perceptions of diversity? Whatever perception, perceiving, the state of having perceived belonging to one who has not attained the absorption and is possessed of the mind element, or possessed of the mind-consciousness element: these are called "perceptions of diversity". He does not attend to these perceptions of diversity. Therefore it is called "with non-attention to perceptions of diversity". ^2-604

605. As to "space is infinite": herein, what is space? Whatever space, that which belongs to space, the void, that which belongs to the void, the opening, that which belongs to the opening, that which is untouched by the four great elements: this is called "space". He fixes and settles the mind on that space, and pervades it as infinite. Therefore it is called "space is infinite". ^2-605

606. As to "the base of infinite space": the states of mind and mental factors belonging to one who has attained, or been reborn through, or dwells happily here and now in the base of infinite space. ^2-606

607. As to "enters and dwells in": whatever gain, attainment, achievement, accomplishment, touching, realizing, and reaching of the base of infinite space there is. ^2-607

608. As to "dwells"... therefore it is called "dwells". ^2-608

609. As to "with the complete transcending of the base of infinite space": he has transcended, thoroughly transcended, and completely transcended this base of infinite space. Therefore it is called "with the complete transcending of the base of infinite space". ^2-609

610. As to "consciousness is infinite": he attends to that very space as touched by consciousness, and pervades it as infinite. Therefore it is called "consciousness is infinite". ^2-610

611. As to "the base of infinite consciousness": the states of mind and mental factors belonging to one who has attained, or been reborn through, or dwells happily here and now in the base of infinite consciousness. ^2-611

612. As to "enters and dwells in": whatever gain, attainment, achievement, accomplishment, touching, realizing, and reaching of the base of infinite consciousness there is. ^2-612

613. As to "dwells"... therefore it is called "dwells". ^2-613

614. As to "with the complete transcending of the base of infinite consciousness": he has transcended, thoroughly transcended, and completely transcended this base of infinite consciousness. Therefore it is called "with the complete transcending of the base of infinite consciousness". ^2-614

615. As to "there is nothing": he develops, un-develops, and does away with that very consciousness, seeing "there is nothing". Therefore it is called "there is nothing". ^2-615

616. As to "the base of nothingness": the states of mind and mental factors belonging to one who has attained, or been reborn through, or dwells happily here and now in the base of nothingness. ^2-616

617. As to "enters and dwells in": whatever gain, attainment, achievement, accomplishment, touching, realizing, and reaching of the base of nothingness there is. ^2-617

618. As to "dwells"... therefore it is called "dwells". ^2-618

619. As to "with the complete transcending of the base of nothingness": he has transcended, thoroughly transcended, and completely transcended this base of nothingness. Therefore it is called "with the complete transcending of the base of nothingness".
As to "neither percipient nor non-percipient": he attends to that very base of nothingness as peaceful, and develops the attainment that has a residue of formations. Therefore it is called "neither percipient nor non-percipient". ^2-619

620. As to "the base of neither perception nor non-perception": the states of mind and mental factors belonging to one who has attained, or been reborn through, or dwells happily here and now in the base of neither perception nor non-perception. ^2-620

621. As to "enters and dwells in": whatever gain, attainment, achievement, accomplishment, touching, realizing, and reaching of the base of neither perception nor non-perception there is. ^2-621

622. As to "dwells": he behaves, conducts himself, maintains himself, keeps himself going, carries on, lives, dwells. Therefore it is called "dwells".
Discourse Classification. ^2-622

#### Abhidhamma Classification ^2-12-2-0

##### Fine-Material-Sphere Wholesome States ^2-12-2-1-0

623. The four absorptions: the first absorption, the second absorption, the third absorption, the fourth absorption. ^2-623

624. Herein, what is the first absorption? Here, at the time when a monk develops the path for rebirth in the fine-material sphere, quite secluded from sense pleasures... he enters and dwells in the first absorption, with the earth device — at that time the five-factored absorption is present: applied thought, sustained thought, joy, happiness, and one-pointedness of mind. This is called "the first absorption". The remaining states are joined with the absorption.
Herein, what is the second absorption? Here, at the time when a monk develops the path for rebirth in the fine-material sphere, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought... he enters and dwells in the second absorption, with the earth device — at that time the three-factored absorption is present: joy, happiness, and one-pointedness of mind. This is called "the second absorption". The remaining states are joined with the absorption.
Herein, what is the third absorption? Here, at the time when a monk develops the path for rebirth in the fine-material sphere, with the fading away of joy... he enters and dwells in the third absorption, with the earth device — at that time the two-factored absorption is present: happiness and one-pointedness of mind. This is called "the third absorption". The remaining states are joined with the absorption.
Herein, what is the fourth absorption? Here, at the time when a monk develops the path for rebirth in the fine-material sphere, with the abandoning of happiness... he enters and dwells in the fourth absorption, with the earth device — at that time the two-factored absorption is present: equanimity and one-pointedness of mind. This is called "the fourth absorption". The remaining states are joined with the absorption.
Tetrad. ^2-624

625. Here, at the time when a monk develops the path for rebirth in the fine-material sphere, quite secluded from sense pleasures... he enters and dwells in the first absorption, with the earth device — at that time the five-factored absorption is present: applied thought, sustained thought, joy, happiness, and one-pointedness of mind. This is called "the first absorption". The remaining states are joined with the absorption.
Here, at the time when a monk develops the path for rebirth in the fine-material sphere, quite secluded from sense pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, he enters and dwells in the second absorption, without applied thought, having only sustained thought, with joy and happiness born of seclusion, with the earth device — at that time the four-factored absorption is present: sustained thought, joy, happiness, and one-pointedness of mind. This is called "the second absorption". The remaining states are joined with the absorption.
Here, at the time when a monk develops the path for rebirth in the fine-material sphere, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought... he enters and dwells in the third absorption, with the earth device — at that time the three-factored absorption is present: joy, happiness, and one-pointedness of mind. This is called "the third absorption". The remaining states are joined with the absorption.
Here, at the time when a monk develops the path for rebirth in the fine-material sphere, with the fading away of joy... he enters and dwells in the fourth absorption, with the earth device — at that time the two-factored absorption is present: happiness and one-pointedness of mind. This is called "the fourth absorption". The remaining states are joined with the absorption.
Here, at the time when a monk develops the path for rebirth in the fine-material sphere, with the abandoning of happiness... he enters and dwells in the fifth absorption, with the earth device — at that time the two-factored absorption is present: equanimity and one-pointedness of mind. This is called "the fifth absorption". The remaining states are joined with the absorption.
Pentad. ^2-625

##### Immaterial-Sphere Wholesome States ^2-12-2-2-0

626. Here, at the time when a monk develops the path for rebirth in the immaterial sphere, with the complete transcending of the base of nothingness, accompanied by the perception of the base of neither perception nor non-perception, with the abandoning of happiness... he enters and dwells in the fourth absorption — at that time the two-factored absorption is present: equanimity and one-pointedness of mind. This is called "the fourth absorption". The remaining states are joined with the absorption. ^2-626

##### World-Transcending Wholesome States ^2-12-2-3-0

627. The four absorptions: the first absorption, the second absorption, the third absorption, the fourth absorption. ^2-627

628. Herein, what is the first absorption? Here, at the time when a monk develops the world-transcending absorption that leads out of the world and leads to the dismantling of accumulation, for the abandoning of wrong views and for reaching the first stage, quite secluded from sense pleasures... he enters and dwells in the first absorption, a difficult practice with slow direct knowledge — at that time the five-factored absorption is present: applied thought, sustained thought, joy, happiness, and one-pointedness of mind. This is called "the first absorption". The remaining states are joined with the absorption.
Herein, what is the second absorption? Here, at the time when a monk develops the world-transcending absorption that leads out of the world and leads to the dismantling of accumulation, for the abandoning of wrong views and for reaching the first stage, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought... he enters and dwells in the second absorption, a difficult practice with slow direct knowledge — at that time the three-factored absorption is present: joy, happiness, and one-pointedness of mind. This is called "the second absorption". The remaining states are joined with the absorption.
Herein, what is the third absorption? Here, at the time when a monk develops the world-transcending absorption that leads out of the world and leads to the dismantling of accumulation, for the abandoning of wrong views and for reaching the first stage, with the fading away of joy... he enters and dwells in the third absorption, a difficult practice with slow direct knowledge — at that time the two-factored absorption is present: happiness and one-pointedness of mind. This is called "the third absorption". The remaining states are joined with the absorption.
Herein, what is the fourth absorption? Here, at the time when a monk develops the world-transcending absorption that leads out of the world and leads to the dismantling of accumulation, for the abandoning of wrong views and for reaching the first stage, with the abandoning of happiness... he enters and dwells in the fourth absorption, a difficult practice with slow direct knowledge — at that time the two-factored absorption is present: equanimity and one-pointedness of mind. This is called "the fourth absorption". The remaining states are joined with the absorption.
Tetrad. ^2-628

629. This is called "the first absorption". The remaining states are joined with the absorption.
Here, at the time when a monk develops the world-transcending absorption that leads out of the world and leads to the dismantling of accumulation, for the abandoning of wrong views and for reaching the first stage, quite secluded from sense pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, he enters and dwells in the second absorption, without applied thought, having only sustained thought, with joy and happiness born of seclusion, a difficult practice with slow direct knowledge — at that time the four-factored absorption is present: sustained thought, joy, happiness, and one-pointedness of mind. This is called "the second absorption". The remaining states are joined with the absorption.
Here, at the time when a monk develops the world-transcending absorption that leads out of the world and leads to the dismantling of accumulation, for the abandoning of wrong views and for reaching the first stage, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought... he enters and dwells in the third absorption, a difficult practice with slow direct knowledge — at that time the three-factored absorption is present: joy, happiness, and one-pointedness of mind. This is called "the third absorption". The remaining states are joined with the absorption.
Here, at the time when a monk develops the world-transcending absorption that leads out of the world and leads to the dismantling of accumulation, for the abandoning of wrong views and for reaching the first stage, with the fading away of joy... he enters and dwells in the fourth absorption, a difficult practice with slow direct knowledge — at that time the two-factored absorption is present: happiness and one-pointedness of mind. This is called "the fourth absorption". The remaining states are joined with the absorption.
Here, at the time when a monk develops the world-transcending absorption that leads out of the world and leads to the dismantling of accumulation, for the abandoning of wrong views and for reaching the first stage, with the abandoning of happiness... he enters and dwells in the fifth absorption, a difficult practice with slow direct knowledge — at that time the two-factored absorption is present: equanimity and one-pointedness of mind. This is called "the fifth absorption". The remaining states are joined with the absorption.
Pentad. ^2-629

##### Fine-Material-Sphere Resultant States ^2-12-2-4-0

630. The four absorptions: the first absorption, the second absorption, the third absorption, the fourth absorption. ^2-630

631. Herein, what is the first absorption? Here, at the time when a monk develops the path for rebirth in the fine-material sphere, quite secluded from sense pleasures... he enters and dwells in the first absorption, with the earth device — at that time contact is present... non-distraction is present. These states are wholesome. Because that very wholesome fine-material-sphere action has been done and accumulated, its result: quite secluded from sense pleasures... he enters and dwells in the first absorption, with the earth device — at that time the five-factored absorption is present: applied thought, sustained thought, joy, happiness, and one-pointedness of mind. This is called "the first absorption". The remaining states are joined with the absorption.
Herein, what is the second absorption? Here, at the time when a monk develops the path for rebirth in the fine-material sphere, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought... he enters and dwells in the second absorption, with the earth device — at that time contact is present... non-distraction is present. These states are wholesome. Because that very wholesome fine-material-sphere action has been done and accumulated, its result: with the stilling of applied and sustained thought... the second absorption... the third absorption... the fourth absorption... the first absorption... he enters and dwells in the fifth absorption, with the earth device — at that time the two-factored absorption is present: equanimity and one-pointedness of mind. This is called "the fifth absorption". The remaining states are joined with the absorption... ^2-631

##### Immaterial-Sphere Resultant States ^2-12-2-5-0

632. Here, at the time when a monk develops the path for rebirth in the immaterial sphere, with the complete transcending of the base of nothingness, accompanied by the perception of the base of neither perception nor non-perception, with the abandoning of happiness... he enters and dwells in the fourth absorption — at that time contact is present... non-distraction is present. These states are wholesome. Because that very wholesome immaterial-sphere action has been done and accumulated, its result: with the complete transcending of the base of nothingness, accompanied by the perception of the base of neither perception nor non-perception, with the abandoning of happiness... he enters and dwells in the fourth absorption — at that time the two-factored absorption is present: equanimity and one-pointedness of mind. This is called "the fourth absorption". The remaining states are joined with the absorption. ^2-632

##### World-Transcending Resultant States ^2-12-2-6-0

633. The four absorptions: the first absorption, the second absorption, the third absorption, the fourth absorption. ^2-633

634. Herein, what is the first absorption? Here, at the time when a monk develops the world-transcending absorption that leads out of the world and leads to the dismantling of accumulation, for the abandoning of wrong views and for reaching the first stage, quite secluded from sense pleasures... he enters and dwells in the first absorption, a difficult practice with slow direct knowledge — at that time contact is present... non-distraction is present. These states are wholesome. Because that very wholesome world-transcending absorption has been done and developed, its result: quite secluded from sense pleasures... he enters and dwells in the first absorption, a difficult practice with slow direct knowledge, which is empty — at that time the five-factored absorption is present: applied thought, sustained thought, joy, happiness, and one-pointedness of mind. This is called "the first absorption". The remaining states are joined with the absorption.
Herein, what is the second absorption? Here, at the time when a monk develops the world-transcending absorption that leads out of the world and leads to the dismantling of accumulation, for the abandoning of wrong views and for reaching the first stage, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought... he enters and dwells in the second absorption, a difficult practice with slow direct knowledge — at that time contact is present... non-distraction is present. These states are wholesome. Because that very wholesome world-transcending absorption has been done and developed, its result: with the stilling of applied and sustained thought... the second absorption... the third absorption... the fourth absorption... the first absorption... he enters and dwells in the fifth absorption, a difficult practice with slow direct knowledge, which is empty — at that time the two-factored absorption is present: equanimity and one-pointedness of mind. This is called "the fifth absorption". The remaining states are joined with the absorption. ^2-634

##### Fine-Material and Immaterial-Sphere Functional States ^2-12-2-7-0

635. The four absorptions: the first absorption, the second absorption, the third absorption, the fourth absorption. ^2-635

636. Herein, what is the first absorption? Here, at the time when a monk develops the fine-material-sphere absorption that is functional, neither wholesome nor unwholesome, nor a result of action, a dwelling happily here and now, quite secluded from sense pleasures... he enters and dwells in the first absorption, with the earth device — at that time the five-factored absorption is present: applied thought, sustained thought, joy, happiness, and one-pointedness of mind. This is called "the first absorption". The remaining states are joined with the absorption.
Herein, what is the second absorption? Here, at the time when a monk develops the fine-material-sphere absorption that is functional, neither wholesome nor unwholesome, nor a result of action, a dwelling happily here and now, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought... the second absorption... the third absorption... the fourth absorption... the first absorption... he enters and dwells in the fifth absorption, with the earth device — at that time the two-factored absorption is present: equanimity and one-pointedness of mind. This is called "the fifth absorption". The remaining states are joined with the absorption. ^2-636

637. Here, at the time when a monk develops the immaterial-sphere absorption that is functional, neither wholesome nor unwholesome, nor a result of action, a dwelling happily here and now, with the complete transcending of the base of nothingness, accompanied by the perception of the base of neither perception nor non-perception, with the abandoning of happiness... he enters and dwells in the fourth absorption — at that time the two-factored absorption is present: equanimity and one-pointedness of mind. This is called "the fourth absorption". The remaining states are joined with the absorption.
Abhidhamma Classification. ^2-637

#### Questions and Answers ^2-12-3-0

638. The four absorptions: here a monk, quite secluded from sense pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the first absorption, accompanied by applied and sustained thought, with joy and happiness born of seclusion... With the stilling of applied and sustained thought, he enters and dwells in the second absorption, which has internal confidence and concentration of mind, is without applied thought and without sustained thought, and has joy and happiness born of concentration... With the fading away of joy, he dwells with equanimity, mindful and clearly comprehending, and experiences happiness with the body; he enters and dwells in the third absorption, of which the noble ones say: "one of equanimity and mindfulness dwells happily"... With the abandoning of happiness and the abandoning of pain, and with the earlier disappearance of gladness and sadness, he enters and dwells in the fourth absorption, which is neither painful nor pleasant, and which has purity of mindfulness through equanimity. ^2-638

639. Of the four absorptions, how many are wholesome, how many unwholesome, how many neutral... how many conflicted, how many peaceful? ^2-639

##### Triads ^2-12-3-1-0

640. May be wholesome, may be neutral. The first three absorptions, apart from the happy feeling arisen in them, are joined with happy feeling; the fourth absorption, apart from the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling arisen in it, is joined with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. May be resultant, may be things that produce a result, may be things that are neither resultant nor things that produce a result. May be clung to and able to be clung to, may be not clung to but able to be clung to, may be not clung to and not able to be clung to. May be undefiled but open to defilement, may be undefiled and not open to defilement. The first absorption, apart from the applied and sustained thought arisen in it, has applied and sustained thought; the other three absorptions are without applied and sustained thought. The first two absorptions, apart from the joy arisen in them, are accompanied by joy; the first three absorptions, apart from the happiness arisen in them, are accompanied by happiness; the fourth absorption, apart from the equanimity arisen in it, is accompanied by equanimity. They are to be abandoned by neither seeing nor development. They are rooted in neither what is to be abandoned by seeing nor what is to be abandoned by development. May lead to accumulation, may lead to dismantling, may neither lead to accumulation nor to dismantling. May be still in training, may be beyond training, may be neither in training nor beyond it. May be exalted, may be measureless. The first three absorptions should not be said to have a limited object or an exalted object; may have a measureless object, or it should not be said that they have a measureless object; the fourth absorption may have a limited object, may have an exalted object, may have a measureless object, or it should not be said that it has a limited object, an exalted object, or a measureless object. May be middling, may be refined. May be fixed in rightness, may be unfixed. The first three absorptions do not have the path as object; may have the path as root, may have the path as dominant factor; it should not be said without qualification that they have the path as root or that they have the path as dominant factor; the fourth absorption may have the path as object, may have the path as root, may have the path as dominant factor; it should not be said without qualification that it has the path as object, that it has the path as root, or that it has the path as dominant factor. May be arisen, may be unarisen, may be bound to arise. May be past, may be future, may be present. The first three absorptions should not be said to have a past object, a future object, or a present object; the fourth absorption may have a past object, may have a future object, may have a present object, or it should not be said that it has a past object, a future object, or a present object. May be internal, may be external, or may be both internal and external. The first three absorptions have an external object; the fourth absorption may have an internal object, may have an external object, may have both an internal and external object, or it should not be said that it has an internal object, an external object, or both an internal and external object. They are invisible and without resistance. ^2-640

##### Pairs ^2-12-3-2-0

641. They are not a root, but are rooted; they are joined with a root. It should not be said that they are both a root and rooted; they are rooted but not themselves a root. It should not be said that they are both a root and joined with a root; they are joined with a root but not themselves a root. They are not a root, but are rooted.
They have conditions. They are conditioned. They are invisible. They offer no resistance. They are immaterial. May be worldly, may be beyond the world. They are knowable by some kinds of consciousness, not knowable by others.
They are not themselves a mental taint. May be subject to mental taints, may be free of mental taints. They are dissociated from a mental taint. It should not be said that they are both a mental taint and subject to mental taints; may be subject to mental taints but not themselves a mental taint, or it should not be said that they are subject to mental taints but not themselves a mental taint. It should not be said that they are both a mental taint and joined with a mental taint, or that they are joined with a mental taint but not themselves a mental taint. May be dissociated from a mental taint and subject to mental taints, may be dissociated from a mental taint and free of mental taints.
They are not themselves a fetter... not themselves a tie... not themselves a flood... not themselves a yoke... not themselves a hindrance... not themselves wrong grasping... They have an object. They are not mind. They are mental factors. They are joined with mind. They are mingled with mind. They originate from mind. They co-arise with mind. They follow mind. They are mingled with mind and originating from mind. They are mingled with mind, originating from mind, and co-arising with mind. They are mingled with mind, originating from mind, and following mind. They are external. They are not derived. May be clung to, may be not clung to.
They are not themselves clinging... not themselves a defilement... They are not to be abandoned by seeing. They are not to be abandoned by development. They are not rooted in what is to be abandoned by seeing. They are not rooted in what is to be abandoned by development. The first absorption, apart from the applied thought arisen in it, has applied thought; the other three absorptions are without applied thought. The first absorption, apart from the sustained thought arisen in it, has sustained thought; the other three absorptions are without sustained thought. The first two absorptions, apart from the joy arisen in them, have joy; the other two absorptions are without joy. The first two absorptions, apart from the joy arisen in them, are accompanied by joy; the other two absorptions are not accompanied by joy. The first three absorptions, apart from the happiness arisen in them, are accompanied by happiness; the fourth absorption is not accompanied by happiness. The fourth absorption, apart from the equanimity arisen in it, is accompanied by equanimity; the first three absorptions are accompanied by equanimity. They do not belong to the sense sphere. May belong to the fine-material sphere, may not belong to the fine-material sphere. The first three absorptions do not belong to the immaterial sphere; the fourth absorption may belong to the immaterial sphere, may not belong to the immaterial sphere. May be included, may be unincluded. May lead out, may not lead out. May be fixed, may be unfixed. May be surpassable, may be unsurpassed. They are peaceful.
Questions and Answers.
The Analysis of the Absorptions is finished. ^2-641

### Analysis of the Immeasurables ^2-13-0

#### Discourse Classification ^2-13-1-0

642. There are four immeasurables. Here a monk dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness; so too the second, so too the third, so too the fourth. Thus above, below, across, everywhere, extending to all as to himself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness that is abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without hostility, without ill will. He dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by compassion; so too the second, so too the third, so too the fourth. Thus above, below, across, everywhere, extending to all as to himself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by compassion that is abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without hostility, without ill will. He dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by sympathetic joy; so too the second, so too the third, so too the fourth. Thus above, below, across, everywhere, extending to all as to himself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by sympathetic joy that is abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without hostility, without ill will. He dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by equanimity; so too the second, so too the third, so too the fourth. Thus above, below, across, everywhere, extending to all as to himself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by equanimity that is abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without hostility, without ill will. ^2-642

##### Loving-kindness ^2-13-1-1-0

643. And how does a monk dwell pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness? Just as, on seeing one person who is dear and pleasing, he would feel loving-kindness for them — in the same way he pervades all beings with loving-kindness.
Herein, what is loving-kindness? Whatever loving-kindness towards beings, feeling of loving-kindness, state of feeling loving-kindness, and liberation of mind through loving-kindness there is: this is called "loving-kindness".
Herein, what is mind? Whatever mind, mind, mental activity, heart, the bright, mind, mind sense-field, mind faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, and the corresponding mind-consciousness element there is: this is called "mind". This mind is accompanied by, co-arisen with, conjoined with, and joined with this loving-kindness. Therefore it is called "with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness". ^2-643

Here, at the time when a monk develops the fine-material-sphere absorption that is functional, neither wholesome nor unwholesome, nor a result of action, a dwelling happily here and now, quite secluded from sense pleasures... he enters and dwells in the first absorption, accompanied by loving-kindness — whatever loving-kindness, feeling of loving-kindness, state of feeling loving-kindness, and liberation of mind through loving-kindness there is at that time: this is called "loving-kindness". The remaining states are joined with loving-kindness.
Herein, what is loving-kindness? Here, at the time when a monk develops the fine-material-sphere absorption that is functional, neither wholesome nor unwholesome, nor a result of action, a dwelling happily here and now, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought... the second absorption... the third absorption... the first absorption... the second absorption... the third absorption... he enters and dwells in the fourth absorption, accompanied by loving-kindness — whatever loving-kindness, feeling of loving-kindness, state of feeling loving-kindness, and liberation of mind through loving-kindness there is at that time: this is called "loving-kindness". The remaining states are joined with loving-kindness. ^2-697

698. Herein, what is compassion... herein, what is sympathetic joy... herein, what is equanimity? Here, at the time when a monk develops the fine-material-sphere absorption that is functional, neither wholesome nor unwholesome, nor a result of action, a dwelling happily here and now, with the abandoning of happiness, with the abandoning of pain... he enters and dwells in the fourth absorption, accompanied by equanimity — whatever equanimity, feeling of equanimity, state of feeling equanimity, and liberation of mind through equanimity there is at that time: this is called "equanimity". The remaining states are joined with equanimity.
