#### Questions and Answers ^2-13-3-0

699. There are four immeasurables. Here a monk dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness, so too the second, so too the third, so too the fourth; thus above, below, across, everywhere, extending to all as to himself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness that is abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without hostility, without ill will. He dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by compassion, so too the second, so too the third, so too the fourth; thus above, below, across, everywhere, extending to all as to himself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by compassion that is abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without hostility, without ill will. He dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by sympathetic joy, so too the second, so too the third, so too the fourth; thus above, below, across, everywhere, extending to all as to himself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by sympathetic joy that is abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without hostility, without ill will. He dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by equanimity, so too the second, so too the third, so too the fourth; thus above, below, across, everywhere, extending to all as to himself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by equanimity that is abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without hostility, without ill will. ^2-699

700. Of the four immeasurables, how many are wholesome, how many unwholesome, how many neutral... how many conflicted, how many peaceful? ^2-700

##### Triads ^2-13-3-1-0

701. May be wholesome, may be neutral. The three immeasurables are joined with pleasant feeling; equanimity is joined with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. May be resultant, may be things that produce a result, may be things that are neither resultant nor things that produce a result. May be clung to and able to be clung to, may be not clung to but able to be clung to. They are undefiled but open to defilement. The three immeasurables may be accompanied by applied and sustained thought, may be without applied thought but having only sustained thought, may be without applied and sustained thought; equanimity is without applied and sustained thought. The three immeasurables may be accompanied by joy, may be accompanied by happiness, not accompanied by equanimity, or it should not be said that they are accompanied by joy; equanimity is accompanied by equanimity. They are to be abandoned by neither seeing nor development. They are rooted in neither what is to be abandoned by seeing nor what is to be abandoned by development. May lead to accumulation, may neither lead to accumulation nor to dismantling. They are neither in training nor beyond training. They are exalted. It should not be said that they have a limited object, an exalted object, or a measureless object. They are middling, unfixed. It should not be said that they have the path as object, that they have the path as root, or that they have the path as dominant factor. May be arisen, may be unarisen, may be bound to arise. May be past, may be future, may be present. It should not be said that they have a past object, a future object, or a present object. May be internal, may be external, may be both internal and external; they have an external object; they are invisible and without resistance. ^2-701

##### Pairs ^2-13-3-2-0

702. Loving-kindness is a root; the other three immeasurables are not a root, but are rooted, and joined with a root. Loving-kindness is both a root and rooted; it should not be said of the other three immeasurables that they are both a root and rooted — they are rooted but not a root. Loving-kindness is both a root and joined with a root; it should not be said of the other three immeasurables that they are both a root and joined with a root — they are joined with a root but not a root. The other three immeasurables are not a root, but are rooted; it should not be said of loving-kindness either that it is not a root but rooted, or that it is not a root and rootless.
They have conditions. They are conditioned. They are invisible. They are without resistance. They are immaterial. They are worldly. They are knowable by some kinds of consciousness, not knowable by others. They are not themselves a mental taint, but are subject to mental taints, and dissociated from a mental taint. It should not be said that they are both a mental taint and subject to mental taints — they are subject to mental taints but not themselves a mental taint. It should not be said that they are both a mental taint and joined with a mental taint — they are joined with a mental taint but not themselves a mental taint. They are dissociated from a mental taint yet subject to mental taints.
They are not themselves a fetter... not themselves a tie... not themselves a flood... not themselves a yoke... not themselves a hindrance... not themselves wrong grasping... They have an object. They are not mind. They are mental factors. They are joined with mind. They are mingled with mind. They originate from mind. They co-arise with mind. They follow mind. They are mingled with mind and originating from mind. They are mingled with mind, originating from mind, and co-arising with mind. They are mingled with mind, originating from mind, and following mind. They are external. They are not derived. May be clung to, may be not clung to.
They are not themselves clinging... not themselves a defilement... They are not to be abandoned by seeing. They are not to be abandoned by development. They are not rooted in what is to be abandoned by seeing. They are not rooted in what is to be abandoned by development. The three immeasurables may be accompanied by applied thought, may be without applied thought; equanimity is without applied thought. The three immeasurables may be accompanied by sustained thought, may be without sustained thought; equanimity is without sustained thought. The three immeasurables may have joy, may be without joy; equanimity is without joy. The three immeasurables may be accompanied by joy, may not be accompanied by joy; equanimity is not accompanied by joy. The three immeasurables are accompanied by happiness; equanimity is not accompanied by happiness. Equanimity is accompanied by equanimity; the three immeasurables are not accompanied by equanimity. They do not belong to the sense sphere. They belong to the fine-material sphere. They do not belong to the immaterial sphere. They are included. They do not lead out. They are unfixed. They are surpassable. They are peaceful.

715. Of the five training rules, how many are wholesome, how many unwholesome, how many neutral... how many conflicted, how many peaceful? ^2-715

##### Triads ^2-14-2-1-0

716. They are only wholesome. They may be joined with pleasant feeling, or may be joined with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. They are things that produce a result. They are not clung to but able to be clung to. They are not defiled but open to defilement. They have applied and sustained thought. They may be accompanied by joy, may be accompanied by happiness, or may be accompanied by equanimity.
They are to be abandoned by neither seeing nor development. They are rooted in neither what is to be abandoned by seeing nor what is to be abandoned by development. They lead to accumulation. They are neither in training nor beyond training. They are limited. They have a limited object. They are middling. They are not fixed. They should not be said to have the path as object, as root, or as dominant factor. They may be arisen, or may be not yet arisen; they should not be said to be "bound to arise". They may be past, may be future, or may be present. They have a present object. They may be internal, may be external, or may be both internal and external. They have an external object. They are invisible and without resistance. ^2-716

##### Pairs ^2-14-2-2-0

717. They are not a root. They are rooted. They are joined with a root. They should not be said to be both a root and rooted; they are rooted but not themselves a root. They should not be said to be both a root and joined with a root; they are joined with a root but not themselves a root. They are not a root, but are rooted. They have conditions. They are conditioned. They are invisible. They offer no resistance. They are immaterial. They are worldly. They are knowable by some kinds of consciousness, not knowable by others.
They are not themselves a mental taint. They are subject to mental taints. They are dissociated from a mental taint. They should not be said to be both a mental taint and subject to mental taints; they are subject to mental taints but not themselves a mental taint. They should not be said to be both a mental taint and joined with a mental taint, or to be joined with a mental taint but not itself a mental taint. They are dissociated from a mental taint but still subject to it. They are not themselves a fetter... not themselves a tie... not themselves a flood... not themselves a yoke... not themselves a hindrance... not themselves wrong grasping... They have an object. They are not mind. They are mental factors. They are joined with mind. They are mingled with mind. They originate from mind. They co-arise with mind. They follow mind. They are mingled with mind and originating from mind. They are mingled with mind, originating from mind, and co-arising with mind. They are mingled with mind, originating from mind, and following mind. They are external. They are not derived. They are not clung to. They are not themselves clinging... not themselves a defilement.
They are not to be abandoned by seeing. They are not to be abandoned by development. They are not rooted in what is to be abandoned by seeing. They are not rooted in what is to be abandoned by development. They have applied thought. They have sustained thought. They may have joy, or may lack joy. They may be accompanied by joy, or may not be accompanied by joy. They may be accompanied by happiness, or may not be accompanied by happiness. They may be accompanied by equanimity, or may not be accompanied by equanimity. They belong to the sense sphere. They do not belong to the fine-material sphere. They do not belong to the immaterial sphere. They are included. They do not lead to liberation. They are not fixed. They are surpassable. They are peaceful.

### Analysis of the Analytical Knowledges ^2-15-0

#### Discourse Classification ^2-15-1-0

##### Summary Section ^2-15-1-1-0

718. There are four analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of principles, the analytical knowledge of language, the analytical knowledge of ready understanding. Knowledge of meaning is the analytical knowledge of meaning; knowledge of principles is the analytical knowledge of principles; knowledge of the language used to express those principles is the analytical knowledge of language; knowledge of these knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready understanding. This is the summary section. ^2-718

##### Truths Section ^2-15-1-2-0

719. There are four analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of principles, the analytical knowledge of language, the analytical knowledge of ready understanding. Knowledge of suffering is the analytical knowledge of meaning; knowledge of the origin of suffering is the analytical knowledge of principles; knowledge of the cessation of suffering is the analytical knowledge of meaning; knowledge of the path leading to the cessation of suffering is the analytical knowledge of principles; knowledge of the language used to express those principles is the analytical knowledge of language; knowledge of these knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready understanding. This is the truths section. ^2-719

This is the causes section. ^2-720

##### Things Section ^2-15-1-4-0

721. This is the things section. ^2-721

##### Scripture Section ^2-15-1-6-0

724. There are four analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of principles, the analytical knowledge of language, the analytical knowledge of ready understanding.
Herein, what is the analytical knowledge of principles? Here a monk knows the teaching — discourses, mixed prose-and-verse, expositions, verses, inspired utterances, "thus it was said" texts, birth stories, marvellous accounts, and question-and-answer texts. This is called "the analytical knowledge of principles". He knows the meaning of each saying: "this is the meaning of this saying, this is the meaning of this saying". This is called "the analytical knowledge of meaning". Knowledge of the language used to express those principles is the analytical knowledge of language. Knowledge of these knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready understanding. This is the scripture section.
Discourse Classification. ^2-724

#### Abhidhamma Classification ^2-15-2-0

##### Wholesome Section ^2-15-2-1-0

725. There are four analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of principles, the analytical knowledge of language, the analytical knowledge of ready understanding.
Which states are wholesome? At the time when a sense-sphere wholesome consciousness has arisen, accompanied by joy, joined with knowledge, having as its object a sight, or... a mental object, or whatever else it may be about — at that time there is contact... there is non-distraction. These states are wholesome. Knowledge of these states is the analytical knowledge of principles. Knowledge of their result is the analytical knowledge of meaning. The language by which those states are designated — knowledge of that expression is the analytical knowledge of language. The knowledge by which one knows those knowledges, thinking: "these knowledges illuminate this meaning" — this is the analytical knowledge of ready understanding. ^2-725

726. There are four analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of principles, the analytical knowledge of language, the analytical knowledge of ready understanding.
Which states are wholesome? At the time when a sense-sphere wholesome consciousness has arisen, accompanied by joy, joined with knowledge, prompted... accompanied by joy, dissociated from knowledge... accompanied by joy, dissociated from knowledge, prompted... accompanied by equanimity, joined with knowledge... accompanied by equanimity, joined with knowledge, prompted... accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge... accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge, prompted, having as its object a sight, or... a mental object, or whatever else it may be about — at that time there is contact... there is non-distraction. These states are wholesome. Knowledge of these states is the analytical knowledge of principles. Knowledge of their result is the analytical knowledge of meaning. The language by which those states are designated — knowledge of that expression is the analytical knowledge of language. The knowledge by which one knows those knowledges, thinking: "these knowledges illuminate this meaning" — this is the analytical knowledge of ready understanding. ^2-726

#### Questions and Answers ^2-15-3-0

747. There are four analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of principles, the analytical knowledge of language, the analytical knowledge of ready understanding. ^2-747

748. Of the four analytical knowledges, how many are wholesome, how many unwholesome, how many neutral... how many conflicted, how many peaceful? ^2-748

##### Triads ^2-15-3-1-0

749. They may be wholesome, or may be neutral. They may be joined with pleasant feeling, or may be joined with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. Three analytical knowledges may be things that produce a result, or may be neither a result nor something that produces a result; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be a result, may be a thing that produces a result, or may be neither a result nor something that produces a result. Three analytical knowledges are not clung to but able to be clung to; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be not clung to but able to be clung to, or may be not clung to and not able to be clung to. Three analytical knowledges are not defiled and not open to defilement; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be not defiled but open to defilement, or may be not defiled and not open to defilement.
Three analytical knowledges have applied and sustained thought; the analytical knowledge of meaning may have applied and sustained thought, may be without applied thought but with sustained thought only, or may be without applied thought and without sustained thought. They may be accompanied by joy, may be accompanied by happiness, or may be accompanied by equanimity. They are to be abandoned by neither seeing nor development. They are rooted in neither what is to be abandoned by seeing nor what is to be abandoned by development.
Three analytical knowledges may lead to accumulation, or may lead to neither accumulation nor dismantling; the analytical knowledge of meaning may lead to accumulation, may lead to dismantling, or may lead to neither accumulation nor dismantling.
Three analytical knowledges are neither in training nor beyond training; the analytical knowledge of meaning may belong to one in training, may belong to one beyond training, or may be neither in training nor beyond training. Three analytical knowledges are limited; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be limited, or may be measureless. The analytical knowledge of language has a limited object; three analytical knowledges may have a limited object, may have an expanded object, or may have a measureless object.
Three analytical knowledges are middling; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be middling, or may be refined. Three analytical knowledges are not fixed; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be fixed in rightness, or may be not fixed. The analytical knowledge of language should not be said to have the path as object, as root, or as dominant factor; the analytical knowledge of meaning does not have the path as object, may have the path as root, may have the path as dominant factor, or should not be said to have the path as root or as dominant factor; two analytical knowledges may have the path as object, do not have the path as root, may have the path as dominant factor, or should not be said to have the path as object or as dominant factor.
Three analytical knowledges may be arisen, or may be not yet arisen; they should not be said to be bound to arise; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be arisen, may be not yet arisen, or may be bound to arise. They may be past, may be future, or may be present. The analytical knowledge of language has a present object; two analytical knowledges may have a past object, may have a future object, or may have a present object; the analytical knowledge of meaning may have a past object, may have a future object, may have a present object, or should not be said to have a past, future, or present object. They may be internal, may be external, or may be both internal and external. The analytical knowledge of language has an external object; three analytical knowledges may have an internal object, may have an external object, or may have both an internal and external object. They are invisible and without resistance. ^2-749

##### Pairs ^2-15-3-2-0

750. They are a root. They are rooted. They are joined with a root. They are both a root and rooted. They are both a root and joined with a root. They should not be said to be not a root but rooted, or to be not a root and rootless.
They have conditions. They are conditioned. They are invisible. They are without resistance. They are immaterial. Three analytical knowledges are worldly; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be worldly, or may be world-transcending. They are knowable by some kinds of consciousness, not knowable by others.
They are not mental taints. Three analytical knowledges are subject to mental taints; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be subject to mental taints, or may be free of mental taints. They are dissociated from mental taints. Three analytical knowledges should not be said to be both a mental taint and subject to mental taints, or to be subject to mental taints but not themselves a mental taint; the analytical knowledge of meaning should not be said to be both a mental taint and subject to mental taints; it may be subject to mental taints but not itself a mental taint, or it should not be said to be subject to mental taints but not itself a mental taint. They should not be said to be both a mental taint and joined with a mental taint, or to be joined with a mental taint but not itself a mental taint. Three analytical knowledges are dissociated from a mental taint but still subject to it; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be dissociated from a mental taint but still subject to it, or may be dissociated from a mental taint and free of it.
They are not fetters... they are not ties... they are not floods... they are not yokes... they are not hindrances... they are not wrong grasping... They have an object. They are not mind. They are mental factors. They are joined with mind. They are mingled with mind. They originate from mind. They co-arise with mind. They follow mind. They are mingled with and originate from mind. They are mingled with, originate from, and co-arise with mind. They are mingled with, originate from, and follow mind. They are external. They are not derived. They are not clung to.
They are not clinging... they are not defilements... they are not to be abandoned by seeing. They are not to be abandoned by development. They are not rooted in what is to be abandoned by seeing. They are not rooted in what is to be abandoned by development. Three analytical knowledges have applied thought; the analytical knowledge of meaning may have applied thought, or may be without applied thought. Three analytical knowledges have sustained thought; the analytical knowledge of meaning may have sustained thought, or may be without sustained thought. They may have joy, or may be without joy. They may be accompanied by joy, or may not be accompanied by joy. They may be accompanied by happiness, or may not be accompanied by happiness. They may be accompanied by equanimity, or may not be accompanied by equanimity. Three analytical knowledges belong to the sense sphere; the analytical knowledge of meaning may belong to the sense sphere, or may not belong to the sense sphere. They do not belong to the fine-material sphere. They do not belong to the immaterial sphere. Three analytical knowledges are included; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be included, or may not be included. Three analytical knowledges do not lead to liberation; the analytical knowledge of meaning may lead to liberation, or may not lead to liberation. Three analytical knowledges are not fixed; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be fixed, or may be not fixed. Three analytical knowledges are surpassable; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be surpassable, or may be unsurpassed. They are peaceful.
Questions and Answers.
The Analysis of the Analytical Knowledges is finished. ^2-750

### Analysis of Knowledge ^2-16-0

#### The Matrix of Ones ^2-16-1-0

751. By way of one kind, the basis of knowledge – the five consciousnesses are not a root, are rootless, are dissociated from roots, have conditions, are conditioned, are immaterial, are worldly, are subject to mental taints, are bound by fetters, are bound by ties, are swept by floods, are bound by yokes, are hindered by hindrances, are wrongly grasped, are subject to clinging, are open to defilement, are neutral, have an object, are not mental factors, are resultant, are clung-to and subject to clinging, are undefiled yet open to defilement, are not accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, are not without applied thought while having only sustained thought, are without applied thought and without sustained thought, are not accompanied by joy, are not to be abandoned by seeing or by development, have no root to be abandoned by seeing or by development, lead neither to accumulation nor to dismantling, are neither in training nor beyond training, are limited, are sense-sphere, are not fine-material-sphere, are not immaterial-sphere, are included, not unincluded, are not fixed, are not emancipating,
have an arisen basis and an arisen object,
(3) have a basis that arose earlier and an object that arose earlier
(4) have an internal basis and an external object
(5) have an unmixed basis and an unmixed object
(6) have different bases and different objects
(7) do not experience one another's field and range
(8) do not arise without adverting
(9) do not arise without attention
(10) do not arise in a fixed order
(11) do not arise simultaneously
(12) do not arise immediately after one another
(13) the five consciousnesses are without active engagement
(14) by means of the five consciousnesses one does not discern anything at all, apart from mere impingement
(15) even immediately after the five consciousnesses, one does not discern anything at all
(16) by means of the five consciousnesses one does not set up any posture
(17) even immediately after the five consciousnesses, one does not set up any posture
(18) by means of the five consciousnesses one does not initiate bodily action or verbal action
(19) even immediately after the five consciousnesses, one does not initiate bodily action or verbal action
(20) by means of the five consciousnesses one does not undertake a wholesome or unwholesome state
(21) even immediately after the five consciousnesses, one does not undertake a wholesome or unwholesome state
(22) by means of the five consciousnesses one does not enter into an attainment or emerge from it
(23) even immediately after the five consciousnesses, one does not enter into an attainment or emerge from it
(24) by means of the five consciousnesses one does not pass away or arise
(25) even immediately after the five consciousnesses, one does not pass away or arise
(26) by means of the five consciousnesses one does not sleep, wake up, or dream
(27) even immediately after the five consciousnesses, one does not sleep, wake up, or dream. Wisdom is what makes clear the true nature of things.

#### The Matrix of Tens ^2-16-10-0

760. By way of ten kinds, the basis of knowledge – the ten powers of the Tathāgata, possessing which the Tathāgata claims the position of the foremost, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets the supreme wheel of the teaching in motion. What are the ten?
(1) Herein, the Tathāgata understands, as it really is, what is possible as possible and what is impossible as impossible. Since the Tathāgata understands, as it really is, what is possible as possible and what is impossible as impossible, this too is a power of the Tathāgata; relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the position of the foremost, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets the supreme wheel of the teaching in motion.
(2) Further, the Tathāgata understands, as it really is, by way of circumstance and by way of cause, the result of undertakings of action, past, future, and present. Since the Tathāgata understands this as it really is, this too is a power of the Tathāgata; relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the position of the foremost, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets the supreme wheel of the teaching in motion.
(3) Further, the Tathāgata understands, as it really is, the practice that leads to every destination. Since the Tathāgata understands this as it really is, this too is a power of the Tathāgata; relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the position of the foremost, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets the supreme wheel of the teaching in motion.
(4) Further, the Tathāgata understands, as it really is, the world with its many and various elements. Since the Tathāgata understands this as it really is, this too is a power of the Tathāgata; relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the position of the foremost, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets the supreme wheel of the teaching in motion.
(5) Further, the Tathāgata understands, as it really is, the various inclinations of beings. Since the Tathāgata understands this as it really is, this too is a power of the Tathāgata; relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the position of the foremost, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets the supreme wheel of the teaching in motion.
(6) Further, the Tathāgata understands, as it really is, the maturity of the faculties of other beings and other persons. Since the Tathāgata understands this as it really is, this too is a power of the Tathāgata; relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the position of the foremost, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets the supreme wheel of the teaching in motion.
(7) Further, the Tathāgata understands, as it really is, the defilement, the purification, and the emergence in respect of the jhānas, the liberations, the concentrations, and the attainments. Since the Tathāgata understands this as it really is, this too is a power of the Tathāgata; relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the position of the foremost, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets the supreme wheel of the teaching in motion.
(8) Further, the Tathāgata understands, as it really is, the recollection of past lives. Since the Tathāgata understands this as it really is, this too is a power of the Tathāgata; relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the position of the foremost, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets the supreme wheel of the teaching in motion.
(9) Further, the Tathāgata understands, as it really is, the passing away and rebirth of beings. Since the Tathāgata understands this as it really is, this too is a power of the Tathāgata; relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the position of the foremost, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets the supreme wheel of the teaching in motion.
(10) Further, the Tathāgata understands, as it really is, the destruction of the mental taints. Since the Tathāgata understands this as it really is, this too is a power of the Tathāgata; relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the position of the foremost, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets the supreme wheel of the teaching in motion. These are the ten powers of the Tathāgata, possessing which the Tathāgata claims the position of the foremost, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets the supreme wheel of the teaching in motion.
Thus, by way of ten kinds, is the basis of knowledge. ^2-760
